title.zh: 卷一百三十九 列傳第八十九: 陸贄
title.raw: 卷一百三十九 列傳第八十九: 陸贄 Volume 139 Biographies 89: Lu Zhi

sentences.zh: 陸贄，字敬輿，蘇州嘉興人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Jingyu, was a native of Jiaxing in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Jingyu, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父侃，溧陽令，以贄貴，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Kan was magistrate of Liyang; because of Zhi's eminence he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Kan had served as magistrate of Liyang; when Zhi rose to prominence, Kan was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 贄少孤，特立不群，頗勤儒學。

translations.literal: Zhi lost his father while young, stood apart from the crowd, and was quite diligent in Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, Zhi held himself apart from others and devoted himself earnestly to classical studies.

sentences.zh: 年十八登進士第，以博學宏詞登科，授華州鄭縣尉。

translations.literal: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination, passed the Broad Learning and Grand Composition examination, and was appointed Wei of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he earned his jinshi degree and also passed the Broad Learning and Grand Composition examination; he was then appointed assistant magistrate of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 罷秩，東歸省母，路由壽州，刺史張鎰有時名，贄往謁之。

translations.literal: When his term ended he went east to visit his mother; passing through Shou Prefecture he called on the prefect Zhang Yi, who enjoyed a reputation at the time.
translations.idiomatic: After his term expired he traveled east to visit his mother. His route took him through Shou Prefecture, where he called on the prefect Zhang Yi, then a man of considerable renown.

sentences.zh: 鎰初不甚知，留三日，再見與語，遂大稱賞，請結忘年之契。

translations.literal: At first Yi did not think much of him; after three days' stay and a second meeting in conversation, Yi greatly praised him and asked to form a friendship across the generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yi initially took little notice of him, but after Zhi stayed three days and they met and talked again, Yi was deeply impressed and asked to become his friend despite the age gap.

sentences.zh: 及辭，遺贄錢百萬，曰：「願備太夫人一日之膳。」

translations.literal: When he took leave, Yi left Zhi a million in cash, saying, "I wish to provide one day's provisions for your honored mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi departed, Yi gave him a million in cash, saying, "Please accept this for your mother's daily needs.

sentences.zh: 贄不納，唯受新茶一串而已，曰：「敢不承君厚意。」

translations.literal: Zhi would not accept it, taking only a single string of new tea, and said, "How dare I not acknowledge your generous intent."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi refused the money and accepted only a single string of fresh tea, saying, "I dare not fail to honor your kindness."

sentences.zh: 又以書判拔萃，選授渭南縣主簿，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He also passed the Outstanding Documents and Judgments selection and was appointed Principal Clerk of Weinan County, then promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the Outstanding Documents and Judgments examination and was appointed principal clerk of Weinan County, then promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮時，素知贄名，乃召為翰林學士，轉祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Dezong was heir apparent he had long known Zhi's name and summoned him as Hanlin Academician, then transferred him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Dezong had long known Zhi's reputation and summoned him as a Hanlin academician, later appointing him vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 贄性忠盡，既居近密，感人主重知，思有以效報，故政或有缺，巨細必陳，由是顧待益厚。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was loyal and exhaustive; once he held a post close and confidential, moved by the sovereign's great trust, he thought to repay it in deed, so whenever policy had a flaw, great or small he must state it, and thereby favor and treatment grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted by nature, Zhi now served in the emperor's inner circle. Grateful for the sovereign's exceptional trust, he sought every means to repay it. Whenever he saw a flaw in policy, large or small, he spoke out without reserve, and the emperor's regard for him deepened accordingly.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，硃泚謀逆，從駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Zhu Ci plotted rebellion and the emperor followed the imperial carriage to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jianzhong era (783), Zhu Ci rebelled, and the court fled with the emperor to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 時天下叛亂，機務填委，征發指蹤，千端萬緒，一日之內，詔書數百。

translations.literal: At that time rebellion filled the realm, urgent business piled up, levies and orders pointed in every direction, a thousand threads and ten thousand ends—in a single day edicts numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion engulfed the empire. State affairs piled up without end; levies, deployments, and orders crisscrossed in every direction. In a single day the court might issue hundreds of edicts.

sentences.zh: 贄揮翰起草，思如泉註，初若不經思慮，既成之後，莫不曲盡事情，中於機會；

translations.literal: Zhi wielded the brush to draft them; thought poured like a spring—at first as if without deliberation, yet once finished none failed to exhaust the matter fully and hit the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi drafted these documents at speed, his thoughts flowing like a spring. His prose seemed effortless, yet every finished text fully grasped the situation and struck precisely the right note.

sentences.zh: 胥吏簡劄不暇，同舍皆伏其能。

translations.literal: Clerks could not keep up with the drafts; colleagues in the same office all submitted to his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks could scarcely keep pace with his drafts, and his colleagues in the Hanlin Academy all marveled at his skill.

sentences.zh: 轉考功郎中，依前充職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Evaluations while continuing his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Bureau of Evaluations while retaining his Hanlin duties.

sentences.zh: 嘗啟德宗曰：「今盜遍天下，輿駕播遷，陛下宜痛自引過，以感動人心。

translations.literal: He once addressed Dezong, saying, "Now bandits fill the realm and the imperial carriage is cast adrift; Your Majesty should deeply blame yourself to move men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He once urged Dezong: "Rebels now hold sway across the empire, and the throne is in exile. Your Majesty should openly acknowledge your faults to move the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 昔成湯以罪己勃興，楚昭以善言復國。

translations.literal: Formerly Cheng Tang rose vigorously by blaming himself; King Zhao of Chu restored his state through good words.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, King Cheng Tang revived his power by confessing his faults, and King Zhao of Chu recovered his kingdom through words of repentance.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能不吝改過，以言謝天下，使書詔無忌，臣雖愚陋，可以仰副聖情，庶令反側之徒，革心向化。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly can be unstinting in reforming faults, with words apologize to the realm, and let written edicts be without reserve, though your servant is foolish and lowly, he can look up to fulfill the sacred intent, and perhaps cause those of unsettled mind to reform their hearts and turn to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will truly repent without reserve, speak frankly to the realm, and issue edicts without holding back, then though I am unworthy, I can help fulfill your intent and perhaps turn those who waver back to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 德宗然之。

translations.literal: Dezong approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 故奉天所下書詔，雖武夫悍卒，無不揮涕感激，多贄所為也。

translations.literal: Therefore the written edicts issued at Fengtian—even fierce soldiers and hardened troops—none failed to weep and be moved; most were Zhi's work.
translations.idiomatic: The edicts issued at Fengtian moved even rough soldiers to tears; most of them were drafted by Zhi.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，議欲以新歲改元。

translations.literal: That winter there was discussion of changing the reign title with the new year.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court debated changing the reign title at the new year.

sentences.zh: 而卜祝之流，皆以國家數鐘百六，凡事宜有變革，以應時數。

translations.literal: Diviners and prayer-officiants alike held that the state's fate had reached the hundred-and-six calamity cycle and all affairs should be changed to accord with the times' numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners and ritual specialists argued that the dynasty had entered an inauspicious cycle in the cosmic order and that reforms were needed to align with the times.

sentences.zh: 上謂贄曰：「往年群臣請上尊號『聖神文武』四字，今緣寇難，諸事並宜改更，眾欲朕舊號之中更加一兩字，其事何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zhi, "In former years the ministers asked to add the honorific of four characters 'Sacred, Divine, Martial, and Civil'; now because of bandit calamity all matters alike should be changed. The multitude wishes to add one or two characters to my old title—what of this matter?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Zhi, "Years ago the ministers asked to bestow on me the honorific 'Sacred, Divine, Martial, and Civil.' Now, with rebellion upon us, many say all things should change—including adding a word or two to my existing title. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 贄奏曰：「尊號之興，本非古制。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized, saying, "The rise of honorific titles was originally not an ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "Honorific titles were never part of ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 行於安泰之日，已累謙沖；

translations.literal: Practiced in days of peace and security, it already burdened modesty and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Even in peaceful times they burdened a ruler's humility.

sentences.zh: 襲乎喪亂之時，尤傷事體。

translations.literal: Continued in times of mourning and disorder, it especially harms the proper form of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: To adopt them amid rebellion and disorder is especially unseemly.

sentences.zh: 今者鑾輿播越，未復宮闈，宗社震驚，尚愆禋祀，中區多梗，大憝猶存。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage is cast adrift, the palace quarters not yet restored; the altars of state are shaken, sacrificial rites still in default; the central regions have many obstructions, the great enemy still exists.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is still in exile, the palace unrestored. The altars of state lie in peril, sacrifices remain neglected, the heartland is beset with troubles, and the great rebel still holds power.

sentences.zh: 此乃人情向背之秋，天意去就之際，陛下宜深自懲勵，收攬群心，痛自貶損，以謝靈譴，不可近從末議，重益美名。」

translations.literal: This is the season when human hearts turn away or return, the juncture when Heaven's intent departs or stays; Your Majesty should deeply admonish and encourage yourself, gather all hearts, painfully diminish yourself to apologize to spiritual reproof—you must not follow petty counsel nearby and again increase fine names."
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment when hearts turn toward or away from the throne, when Heaven's favor hangs in the balance. Your Majesty should discipline yourself, win back the people's loyalty, and humble yourself to answer Heaven's rebuke—not heed petty counsel and pile up empty titles."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿所奏陳，雖理體甚切，然時運必須小有改跡，亦不可執滯，卿更思量。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What you have memorialized, though its principle and form are very apt, yet the times' fortune must have a small change of trace—it cannot be held rigid; consider further."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your reasoning is sound, but the times demand some outward change. One cannot be inflexible. Consider the matter again."

sentences.zh: 贄曰：「古之人君稱號，或稱皇稱帝，或稱王，但一字而已。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Ancient rulers' titles—some called themselves Huang, some Di, some Wang—only a single character.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "Ancient rulers called themselves Huang, Di, or Wang—never more than a single word.

sentences.zh: 至暴秦，乃兼皇帝二字，後代因之。

translations.literal: It reached the violent Qin, which then combined the two characters Huang and Di; later ages followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Only under the tyrannical Qin were the two characters Huang and Di combined, and later dynasties followed suit.

sentences.zh: 及昏僻之君，乃有聖劉、天元之號。

translations.literal: When it came to benighted and perverse rulers, then arose titles like Sacred Liu and Celestial Prime.
translations.idiomatic: Only debased rulers took such titles as Sacred Liu or Celestial Prime.

sentences.zh: 是知人主輕重，不在自稱，崇其號無補於徽猷；

translations.literal: From this one knows that a ruler's weight lies not in what he calls himself; exalting his title does not aid his excellent plans.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's stature does not depend on what he calls himself. Adding to his title does nothing for good governance.

sentences.zh: 損其名不傷其德美。

translations.literal: Diminishing his name does not harm his virtue and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Reducing his title does not diminish his virtue.

sentences.zh: 然而損之有謙光稽古之善，崇之獲矜能納諂之譏，得失不侔，居然可辨。

translations.literal: Yet to diminish has the good of modest radiance and examining antiquity; to exalt obtains the reproach of pride in ability and accepting flattery—the gain and loss do not match, clearly distinguishable.
translations.idiomatic: To diminish one's title shows humility and respect for antiquity; to exalt it invites the charge of pride and flattery. The difference between gain and loss is plain.

sentences.zh: 況今時遭迍否，事屬傾危，尤宜懼思，以自貶抑。

translations.literal: Moreover, now the times meet obstruction and denial, affairs belong to tipping peril—especially one should fear and reflect, to diminish oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in this time of obstruction and peril, you should all the more reflect in fear and humble yourself.

sentences.zh: 必也俯稽術數，須有變更。

translations.literal: If you must bow to examine numerology and fate, there must be change.
translations.idiomatic: If you must heed numerology and fate, change is still required.

sentences.zh: 與其增美稱而失人心，不若黜舊號以祗天戒。

translations.literal: Rather than increase fine titles and lose men's hearts, better to dismiss the old title to respect Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: Better to set aside your old title and heed Heaven's warning than to add grand titles and lose the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 天時人事，理必相符，人既好謙，天亦助順。

translations.literal: Heaven's seasons and human affairs—principle must correspond; when men already love modesty, Heaven also aids compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's will and human affairs must align. When men love humility, Heaven aids those who submit.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能斷自宸鑒，煥發德音，引咎降名，深示刻責，惟謙與順，一舉而二美從之。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly can decide from the imperial mirror, send forth radiant virtuous words, draw blame and lower your name, deeply show severe self-reproach—only modesty and compliance, one act and two beauties follow."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will judge for yourself, issue words of virtue, confess fault and lower your title, and show deep self-reproach, then in one act you will gain both humility and submission to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 德宗從之，但改興元年號而已。

translations.literal: Dezong followed this, changing only to the Xingyuan reign title.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong accepted his advice and changed only the reign title to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗倉皇出幸，府藏委棄，凝冽之際，士眾多寒，服禦之外，無尺縑丈帛。

translations.literal: At first Dezong fled in haste; treasury stores were abandoned. In biting cold, troops and masses mostly suffered cold; beyond clothing for the ruler, not a foot of silk or a bolt of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first fled in haste, the treasury was abandoned. In the bitter cold the soldiers had little to wear; beyond the emperor's own garments there was scarcely a scrap of silk or cloth.

sentences.zh: 及賊泚解圍，諸籓貢奉繼至，乃於奉天行在貯貢物於廊下，仍題曰「瓊林」、「大盈」二庫名。

translations.literal: When the bandit Ci lifted the siege, tribute from the various fiefs arrived in succession; then at the Fengtian mobile court they stored tribute goods under the corridor and still labeled them with the two storehouse names Jade Grove and Great Abundance.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's siege was lifted, tribute poured in from the provinces. At the Fengtian encampment the gifts were stored in the corridors and labeled with the names of two treasuries: Jade Grove and Great Abundance.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhi remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 「瓊林」、「大盈」，自古悉無其制，傳諸耆舊之說，皆云創自開元。

translations.literal: "Jade Grove" and "Great Abundance"—from antiquity there was entirely no such institution; transmitted among elders' accounts, all say they were created from the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: "The treasuries called Jade Grove and Great Abundance have no precedent in antiquity. Elders say they were created in the Kaiyuan era."

sentences.zh: 貴臣貪權，飾巧求媚，乃言：「郡邑貢賦所用，盍各區分：賦稅當委於有司，以給經用；

translations.literal: Noble ministers greedy for power, adorning craft to seek favor, then said: "The uses of commandery and county tribute and levies—why not each be divided? Levies and taxes should be entrusted to the responsible offices to supply regular expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers, greedy for influence and skilled in flattery, proposed: "Let us separate the uses of local tribute: taxes should go to the regular offices for state expenses,

sentences.zh: 貢獻宜歸於天子，以奉私求。」

translations.literal: Tribute offerings should return to the Son of Heaven to serve private desires.
translations.idiomatic: while gifts of tribute should belong to the Son of Heaven for his private use.

sentences.zh: 玄宗悅之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was pleased with this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong approved.

sentences.zh: 新是二庫，蕩心侈欲，萌柢於茲，迨乎失邦，終以餌寇。

translations.literal: Newly establishing these two storehouses, dissolving the heart in extravagant desire—the sprout and root began here; when it reached losing the realm, in the end it became bait for bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Thus were these two treasuries born, planting the seeds of dissolute desire. In the end the dynasty lost the realm and fed its enemies.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「貨悖而入，必悖而出。」

translations.literal: The Record says: "Wealth that enters perversely must perversely go out.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, "Wealth gained unjustly will be lost unjustly.

sentences.zh: 豈其效歟！

translations.literal: Was this not its effect!
translations.idiomatic: Was this not exactly what followed!

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣位之初，務遵理道，敦行儉約，斥遠貪饕。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first succeeded to the throne, you strove to follow the Way of principle, earnestly practiced frugality and restraint, and repelled the greedy and gluttonous from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you devoted yourself to right governance, practiced frugality, and kept the greedy at a distance.

sentences.zh: 雖內庫舊藏，未歸太府，而諸方曲獻，不入禁闈，清風肅然，海內丕變。

translations.literal: Although old stores of the inner treasury had not returned to the Grand Treasury, yet regional partial offerings did not enter the forbidden quarters; pure wind was solemn, within the seas greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the inner treasury's old hoards had not yet been returned to the Grand Treasury, regional gifts no longer entered the palace. A refreshing discipline prevailed, and the realm was transformed.

sentences.zh: 近以寇逆亂常，鑾輿外幸，既屬憂危之運，宜增儆勵之誠。

translations.literal: Recently because bandit rebels disturbed the norm and the imperial carriage went abroad, this already belongs to a fortune of worry and peril—you should increase vigilant encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Now rebellion has thrown the realm into disorder and the throne is in exile. In such a time of peril you should redouble vigilance and restraint.

sentences.zh: 臣昨奉使軍營，出經行殿，忽睹右廓之下，榜列二庫之名，戄然若驚，不識所以。

translations.literal: Yesterday your servant, on mission to the army camps, going out passed the traveling palace and suddenly saw under the right corridor placards listing the two storehouse names—startled as if in shock, not knowing the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, on mission to the army camps, I passed the traveling palace and suddenly saw under the right corridor placards bearing the names of those two treasuries. I was struck with alarm and could not understand why.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 天衢尚梗，師旅方殷，痛心呻吟之聲，噢咻未息；

translations.literal: Heaven's thoroughfares are still blocked, armies and hosts are just now pressing; sounds of pained hearts and groaning, gasping and moaning have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The roads are still blocked, the armies still engaged. The wounded groan and cry without cease.

sentences.zh: 忠勤戰守之效，賞賚未行。

translations.literal: The effects of loyal diligence in battle and defense—rewards and gifts have not been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fought loyally have yet to receive their rewards.

sentences.zh: 諸道貢珍，遽私別庫，萬目所視，孰能忍情？

translations.literal: Tribute treasures from the various circuits are hastily set apart in private storehouses—ten thousand eyes behold this; who can bear the feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from the provinces is suddenly set aside in private treasuries before ten thousand watching eyes. Who can bear it?

sentences.zh: 竊揣軍情，或生觖望，或忿形謗讟，或醜肆謳謠，頗含思亂之情，亦有悔忠之意。

translations.literal: Privately I gauge army sentiment: some may breed divided hopes, some show resentment in slander and abuse, some ugly and unrestrained in ballads and songs—quite containing thoughts of disorder, also having mind to regret loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the army may grow resentful, break into open slander, or spread ugly songs of discontent. Some already harbor thoughts of rebellion; others regret their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 是知氓俗昏鄙，識昧高卑，不可以尊極臨，而可以誠義感。

translations.literal: From this one knows that common custom is benighted and base, knowledge dim to high and low—you cannot with utmost honor approach them, but can with sincere righteousness move them.
translations.idiomatic: The common people are dull and cannot judge high from low. They cannot be won by displays of majesty, but they can be moved by sincerity and justice.

sentences.zh: 頃者六師初降，百物無儲，外扞兇徒，內防危堞，晝夜不息，殆將五旬。

translations.literal: Recently when the Six Armies first submitted, a hundred things had no stores; outwardly resisting fierce factions, inwardly defending perilous ramparts—day and night without rest, nearly fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armies first arrived, there were no stores of any kind. Outwardly they fought the rebels; inwardly they defended the walls. Day and night without rest—for nearly fifty days.

sentences.zh: 凍餓交侵，死傷相枕，畢命同力，竟夷大艱。

translations.literal: Cold and hunger together assailed; dead and wounded pillowed one another; exhausting life with united strength, in the end they leveled the great hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and hunger assailed them together; the dead and wounded lay piled upon one another. Yet they gave their all in common effort and at last overcame the great peril.

sentences.zh: 良以陛下不厚其身，不私其欲，絕甘以同卒伍，輟食以啖功勞。

translations.literal: Truly because Your Majesty did not enrich his person, did not privatize his desires, cut off sweetness to share with the ranks, stopped food to feed merit and toil.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Your Majesty did not pamper himself or indulge his desires—he gave up delicacies to share with the ranks and went without food to feed those who had earned it.

sentences.zh: 無猛制人而不攜，懷所感也；

translations.literal: Without fierce control yet men not alienated—this was what they felt in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Without harsh discipline the men did not desert you, because they felt your care.

sentences.zh: 無厚賞士而不怨，悉所無也。

translations.literal: Without thick rewards yet soldiers not resentful—all because there was nothing to give.
translations.idiomatic: Without rich rewards they did not complain, because you had nothing to give.

sentences.zh: 今者攻圍已解，衣食已豐，而謗讟方興，軍情稍沮，豈不以勇夫常性，嗜貨矜功，其患難既與之同憂，而好樂不與之同利，茍異恬默，能無怨咨！

translations.literal: Now the siege is already lifted, clothing and food already abundant, yet slander and abuse are just rising, army sentiment somewhat discouraged—is it not because brave men's constant nature loves goods and prizes achievement? Their hardship they already shared in worry with you, yet pleasure and profit they do not share with you in benefit; if this differs from calm silence, how can there be no resentment and complaint!
translations.idiomatic: Now the siege is lifted and food and clothing are plentiful, yet slander rises and army morale falters. Brave men by nature love gain and prize merit. They shared your hardship but do not share your ease. How can they remain silent without complaint?

sentences.zh: 此理之常，故不足怪。

translations.literal: This is the constant of principle—therefore not enough to marvel at.
translations.idiomatic: This is only human nature and is not to be wondered at.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「財散則民聚。」

translations.literal: The Record says: "When wealth is scattered, the people gather.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, "When wealth is dispersed, the people gather.

sentences.zh: 豈其效歟！

translations.literal: Was this not its effect!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the lesson!

sentences.zh: 陛下天資英聖，見善必遷，是將化蓄怨為銜恩，反過差為至當，促殄遺寇，永垂鴻名，大聖應機，固當不俟終日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's Heaven-endowed talent is heroic and sage; seeing good you must turn—this will transform stored resentment into cherishing grace, reverse excess into utmost propriety, hasten the extermination of remaining bandits, forever trail great fame; the great sage responding to the moment—solidly should not wait for the day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is gifted and sage, and turns to good at once. You can turn stored resentment into gratitude, correct error into right conduct, destroy the remaining rebels, and win lasting fame. A great sage acts when the moment calls—surely he need not wait even a day.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之，令去其題署。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this, ordering the labels removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered the placards removed.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，李懷光異志已萌，欲激怒諸軍，上表論諸軍衣糧薄，神策衣糧厚，厚薄不均，難以驅戰，意在撓沮進軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Li Huai'guang's divergent intent had already sprouted; wishing to enrage the various armies, he memorialized that the various armies' clothing and grain rations were thin while the Shence Army's were thick—uneven thick and thin, hard to drive to battle—his intent being to thwart and discourage the advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan (784), Li Huai'guang's disloyalty had already shown itself. Seeking to provoke the other armies, he memorialized that their rations of clothing and grain were meager while the Shence Army's were ample—unequal treatment, he claimed, made united campaigning impossible. His aim was to obstruct the advance.

sentences.zh: 李晟密奏，恐其有變，上憂之，遣贄使懷光軍宣諭。

translations.literal: Li Sheng secretly memorialized, fearing he would have a change; the emperor was worried and sent Zhi as envoy to Huai'guang's army to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng secretly warned that Huai'guang might rebel. The emperor was alarmed and sent Zhi to his camp to deliver the imperial message.

sentences.zh: 使還，贄奏事曰：

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, Zhi reported on affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhi reported to the throne:

sentences.zh: 賊泚稽誅，保聚宮苑，勢窮援絕，引日偷生。

translations.literal: The bandit Ci awaits execution, holding and gathering in the palace parks; his power exhausted, aid cut off, drawing out days to steal life.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhu Ci awaits punishment, holed up in the palace grounds. His strength is spent, his allies gone; he merely prolongs his days.

sentences.zh: 懷光總仗順之軍，乘制勝之氣，鼓行芟翦，易若摧枯。

translations.literal: Huai'guang commands armies that rely on righteousness, rides the breath of assured victory—drumming forward to mow and cut, easy as snapping dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang commands armies loyal to the throne and holds the advantage. He need only march forward to cut Zhu Ci down as easily as breaking dry wood.

sentences.zh: 而乃寇奔不追，師老不用，諸帥每欲進取，懷光輒沮其謀。

translations.literal: Yet he does not pursue when the bandit flees; the army grows old and is not used; whenever the various commanders wish to advance, Huai'guang always thwarts their plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he does not pursue the fleeing enemy. His army grows idle. Whenever the other commanders wish to advance, Huai'guang blocks them.

sentences.zh: 據茲事情，殊不可解。

translations.literal: According to these circumstances, especially incomprehensible.
translations.idiomatic: On these grounds his conduct is utterly inexplicable.

sentences.zh: 陛下意在全護，委曲聽從，觀其所為，亦未知感。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's intent is to protect him wholly, following him with accommodation—observing his conduct, he also does not seem to know gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has sought to protect him and indulged his wishes, yet he shows no gratitude.

sentences.zh: 若不別為規略，漸相制持，唯以姑息求安，終恐變故難測。

translations.literal: If you do not separately devise strategy and gradually restrain one another, seeking only ease through indulgence, in the end I fear unforeseen change will be hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you adopt another strategy and gradually restrain him, seeking only temporary peace through indulgence, I fear an unforeseen crisis will arise.

sentences.zh: 此誠事機危迫之秋也，故不可以尋常容易處之。

translations.literal: This is truly the season when the moment's opportunity is perilously pressing—therefore one cannot treat it with the ordinary and easy.
translations.idiomatic: This is a moment of grave urgency and cannot be handled with ordinary ease.

sentences.zh: 今李晟奏請移軍，適遇臣銜命宣慰，懷光偶論此事，臣遂泛問所宜，懷光乃云：「李晟既欲別行，某亦都不要藉。」

translations.literal: Now Li Sheng memorializes requesting to move the army; it happened to meet your servant bearing orders to proclaim comfort. Huai'guang chanced to discuss this matter; your servant then broadly asked what was fitting. Huai'guang then said: "Since Li Sheng wishes to march separately, I also need no support at all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng has now asked to move his army. It happened that I was on mission to comfort the troops when Huai'guang raised the matter. I asked his view, and he said, "If Li Sheng wishes to march separately, I need no support from him at all.

sentences.zh: 臣猶慮有翻覆，因美其軍強盛。

translations.literal: Your servant still feared reversal and therefore praised his army as strong and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he might change his mind, I praised the strength of his army.

sentences.zh: 懷光大自矜誇，轉有輕晟之意。

translations.literal: Huai'guang greatly prided himself and boasted, turning to have mind to slight Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang swelled with pride and showed contempt for Li Sheng.

sentences.zh: 臣又從容問云：「昨發離行在之日，未知有此商量；

translations.literal: Your servant again calmly asked, saying: "When I set out leaving the mobile court yesterday, I did not know of this consultation.
translations.idiomatic: I then asked calmly, "When I left the imperial camp yesterday, this matter had not been discussed.

sentences.zh: 今日從此卻回，或恐聖旨顧問，事之可否，決定何如？」

translations.literal: Today returning from here, I fear the sacred edict may inquire—whether the affair can be done or not, how is it decided?
translations.idiomatic: If I return now, the emperor may inquire. Has the matter been decided, or not?

sentences.zh: 懷光已肆輕言，不可中變，遂云：「恩命許去，事亦無妨。」

translations.literal: Huai'guang had already let loose light words and could not change midway; he then said: "If grace and command permit departure, the affair also has no obstacle."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang had spoken rashly and could not take it back. He said, "If the emperor permits it, there is no objection."

sentences.zh: 要約再三，非不詳審，雖欲追悔，固難為詞。

translations.literal: The essential agreement was repeated three times—not inattentive or uncareful; though he wishes to regret and turn back, solidly it is hard to find words.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated his assent several times, clearly and deliberately. Though he may wish to retract it, he can hardly find words to do so.

sentences.zh: 伏望即以李晟表出付中書，敕下依奏，別賜懷光手詔，示以移軍事由。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will immediately take Li Sheng's memorial out and deliver it to the Secretariat, issue an edict down according to the memorial, and separately bestow on Huai'guang a handwritten edict showing the reasons for moving the army.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to send Li Sheng's memorial to the Secretariat, issue an edict approving it, and separately send Huai'guang a handwritten edict explaining the reasons for the troop movement.

sentences.zh: 其手詔大意云：「昨得李晟奏，請移軍城東以分賊勢。

translations.literal: The handwritten edict's general sense would say: "Yesterday I received Li Sheng's memorial requesting to move the army east of the city to divide the bandits' power.
translations.idiomatic: The handwritten edict might read in substance: "Yesterday I received Li Sheng's memorial asking to move his army east of the city to divide the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 朕緣未知利害，本欲委卿商量，適會陸贄從彼宣慰回，雲見卿論敘軍情，語及於此，仍言許去，事亦無妨，遂敕本軍允其所請。

translations.literal: We, not yet knowing advantage and harm, originally wished to entrust this to you for consultation; it happened to meet Lu Zhi returning from proclaiming comfort there, who said he saw you discuss and narrate army sentiment, words reaching this point, still saying permission to go—the affair also has no obstacle—thereupon We ordered your original army to grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing the full implications, I meant to consult you. Lu Zhi has just returned from your camp and reports that in discussing the army's situation you agreed that Li Sheng's move would be acceptable. I have therefore ordered Li Sheng's request granted.

sentences.zh: 卿宜授以謀略，分路夾攻，務使葉齊，克平寇孽。」

translations.literal: You should grant him strategy, divide routes and attack from both sides, strive to make efforts together, conquer and level the bandit spawn.
translations.idiomatic: You should give him your counsel, attack by separate routes, and together destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 如此詞婉而直，理當而明，雖蓄異端，何由起怨？

translations.literal: Thus the words are tactful yet direct, principle fitting yet clear—even if he harbors divergent intent, whence would resentment arise?
translations.idiomatic: Such words would be tactful yet direct, reasonable and clear. Even if he harbors disloyalty, how could he take offense?

sentences.zh: 臣初奉使諭旨，本緣糧料不均，偶屬移軍，事相諧會。

translations.literal: When your servant first received mission to proclaim the intent, it was originally because of uneven grain rations; it happened to coincide with moving the army—the affairs harmoniously met.
translations.idiomatic: My original mission concerned unequal rations. The question of moving troops arose by chance, and the two matters fell conveniently together.

sentences.zh: 又幸懷光詭對，且無阻絕之言，機宜合並。

translations.literal: Also fortunately Huai'guang's crafty reply had no words of obstruction—the opportune moment should be joined.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Huai'guang answered evasively and did not refuse outright. The opportunity should be seized at once.

sentences.zh: 若有幽贊，一失其便，後何可追，幸垂裁察！

translations.literal: If there is hidden approval and one loses this convenience, afterward how can it be pursued? I hope you will deign to judge and examine!
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven favors us and we miss this chance, it cannot be recovered. I beg Your Majesty to decide!

sentences.zh: 德宗初望懷光回意破賊，故晟屢奏移軍不許；

translations.literal: Dezong at first hoped Huai'guang would turn his mind and break the bandits, so Sheng's repeated memorials to move the army were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong had initially hoped Huai'guang would return to loyalty and destroy the rebels, so Li Sheng's repeated requests to move his army were denied.

sentences.zh: 及贄縷陳懷光反狀，乃可晟之奏，遂移軍東渭橋。

translations.literal: When Zhi in detail set forth Huai'guang's rebellious signs, then Sheng's memorial was approved, and the army was moved to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi detailed Huai'guang's signs of rebellion, the emperor approved Li Sheng's request, and the army was moved to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 而鄜坊節度李建徽、神策行營陽惠元猶在咸陽，贄慮懷光並建徽等軍，又奏曰：

translations.literal: Meanwhile Fufang Military Governor Li Jianhui and Shence Mobile Camp Commander Yang Huiyuan were still at Xianyang; Zhi, fearing Huai'guang would absorb Jianhui's and the other armies, again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Jianhui, military governor of Fufang, and Yang Huiyuan of the Shence mobile camp were still at Xianyang. Fearing that Huai'guang would absorb their armies, Lu Zhi memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 懷光當管師徒，足以獨制兇寇，逗留未進，抑有他由。

translations.literal: Huai'guang commands the army under his charge, sufficient alone to restrain the fierce bandits; his lingering without advancing surely has another cause.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang commands enough troops to subdue the rebels on his own. If he has lingered without advancing, there must be another reason.

sentences.zh: 所患太強，不資傍助。

translations.literal: What one worries about is that he is too strong, not that he lacks help from others.
translations.idiomatic: The concern is not that he lacks support, but that he is too strong.

sentences.zh: 比者又遣李晟、李建徽、陽惠元三節度之眾附麗其營，無益成功，只憂生事。

translations.literal: Recently Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan—the armies of three military governors—were again sent to attach to his camp; it does no good for success, only raises worry of stirring trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan—the forces of three military governors—were attached to his camp. This will not help achieve victory; it will only provoke trouble.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 四軍懸壘，群帥異心，論勢力則懸絕高卑，據職名則不相統屬。

translations.literal: Four armies stand in separate camps, their commanders of different minds; in strength they are vastly unequal, and by office and title they do not belong to one chain of command.
translations.idiomatic: Four armies camp apart, and their commanders are at odds. In strength they are vastly unequal, and in rank none is subordinate to another.

sentences.zh: 懷光輕晟等兵微位下，而忿其制不從心。

translations.literal: Huai'guang disdains Sheng and the others for their small armies and low rank, and resents that he cannot fully command them.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang looks down on Li Sheng and the others for their weaker forces and lower rank, and resents that he cannot fully command them.

sentences.zh: 晟等疑懷光養寇蓄奸，而怨其事多陵己。

translations.literal: Sheng and the others suspect Huai'guang of harboring bandits and hoarding treachery, and resent that his affairs often encroach on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng and the others suspect Huai'guang of deliberately sparing the enemy and harboring treachery, and resent his habit of riding roughshod over them.

sentences.zh: 端居則互防飛謗，欲戰則遞恐分功，齟齬不和，嫌釁遂構，俾之同處，必不兩全。

translations.literal: At rest they mutually guard against slander; wishing to fight, they each fear sharing merit. Discord and ill will build; placed together, both cannot be preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: In camp they trade slander; in battle each fears the other will steal credit. Mutual distrust breeds conflict, and if they remain together, neither side can survive intact.

sentences.zh: 強者惡積而後亡，弱者勢危而先覆，覆亡之禍，翹足可期。

translations.literal: The strong, hatred accumulated, perish afterward; the weak, position perilous, are overturned first; the calamity of ruin can be awaited with heels raised.
translations.idiomatic: The stronger will be destroyed only after hatred has built up; the weaker, more endangered, will fall first. Their ruin is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 舊寇未平，新患方起，憂嘆所切，實堪疚心。

translations.literal: The old bandits are not yet pacified, new trouble is just rising; the worry and sigh of what cuts close truly can afflict the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The old enemy is not yet subdued and a new threat is already rising. The anguish of this situation is truly hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 太上消慝於未萌，其次救失於始兆，況乎事情已露，禍難垂成，委而不謀，何以制亂？

translations.literal: The highest removes blight before it sprouts; next saves mistakes at the first sign; how much more when the matter is already exposed and calamity about to be complete—entrust without planning, how govern disorder?
translations.idiomatic: The wise eliminate evil before it takes root; the next best remedy is at the first sign of trouble. When the danger is already exposed and disaster imminent, how can we refuse to act and still hope to control the chaos?

sentences.zh: 李晟見機慮變，先請移軍就東，建徽、惠元，勢轉孤弱，為其吞噬，理在必然。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, seeing the moment and considering change, first requested to move the army east; Jianhui and Huiyuan, power turning isolated and weak, will be swallowed by him—reason lies in inevitability.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng saw what was coming and asked to move his army east. Jianhui and Huiyuan, left isolated and weak, will inevitably be swallowed up by Huai'guang.

sentences.zh: 他日雖有良圖，亦恐不能自拔，拯其危急，唯在此時。

translations.literal: Another day though there be good plans, I fear he still cannot extract himself; saving their urgent peril lies only in this moment.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they devise a better plan later, they may not escape in time. To save them, we must act now.

sentences.zh: 今因李晟願行，便遣合軍同往，托言晟兵素少，慮為賊泚所邀，藉此兩軍，叠為掎角。

translations.literal: Now, taking Li Sheng's wish to go, send the combined armies to go together; under pretext that Sheng's troops are always few, fearing interception by the bandit Zhu Ci, by means of these two armies, layered as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Use Li Sheng's request as pretext to send all three armies east together. Say that Li Sheng's force is too small and might be intercepted by Zhu Ci's rebels, and that the other two armies will support him in a coordinated pincer.

sentences.zh: 仍先諭旨，密使促裝，詔書至營，即日進路。

translations.literal: Still first proclaim the intent, secretly send orders to hasten packing; when the edict reaches camp, that same day march the route.
translations.idiomatic: First send secret orders to prepare to march; when the edict reaches camp, they should move that same day.

sentences.zh: 懷光意雖不欲，然亦計無所施。

translations.literal: Huai'guang in mind though unwilling, yet also finds no measure to apply.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang will dislike it, but will have no way to stop it.

sentences.zh: 是謂先人有奪人之心，疾雷不及掩耳者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called the first striker having a heart to seize from others—swift thunder does not reach before covering the ears.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the ancients meant by striking first: thunder before one can cover one's ears.

sentences.zh: 夫制軍馭將，所貴見情，離合疾徐，各有宜適。

translations.literal: As for controlling armies and driving generals, what is prized is seeing the circumstances; separation and union, haste and delay, each has its fitting place.
translations.idiomatic: In commanding armies and managing generals, what matters is reading the situation. Whether to unite or divide, to act quickly or slowly—each has its proper moment.

sentences.zh: 當離者合之則召亂，當合者離之則寡功；

translations.literal: Those who should be separated, if joined will summon disorder; those who should be joined, if separated will have scant achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Joining those who should be kept apart invites chaos; separating those who should act together diminishes their effectiveness.

sentences.zh: 當疾而徐則失機，當徐而疾則漏策。

translations.literal: When haste is called for, if slow then lose the moment; when delay is called for, if hasty then leak the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Moving too slowly when speed is needed loses the opportunity; acting too quickly when caution is needed ruins the plan.

sentences.zh: 得其要，契其時，然後舉無敗謀，措無危勢。

translations.literal: Obtaining its essentials, matching its time, then raising plans none fail, placing measures none perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the essential point and act at the right moment, and no plan will fail and no move will create danger.

sentences.zh: 而今者屯兵而不肯為用，聚將而罔能葉心，自為鯨鯢，變在朝夕。

translations.literal: Yet now armies are encamped yet unwilling to be used, generals gathered yet unable to unite in heart—they make themselves whales and narwhals; change lies within morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Now troops are assembled but will not cooperate, and generals are gathered but cannot unite. They are turning into mortal enemies, and disaster may strike at any moment.

sentences.zh: 留之不足以相制，徒長歷階；

translations.literal: Keeping them is insufficient to restrain each other, only vainly lengthening step-by-step ascent.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping them together will not allow them to check one another; it will only escalate the danger.

sentences.zh: 析之各競於擅能，或成勛績。

translations.literal: Dividing them, each competes in exclusive ability, perhaps achieving merit and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Separating them, each may strive to prove himself and perhaps achieve merit.

sentences.zh: 事有必應，斷無可疑。

translations.literal: The matter has what must be answered; decisively nothing doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: This must be done; there is no room for doubt.

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：「卿之所料極善。

translations.literal: Dezong said: "What you anticipate is extremely good.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said, "Your assessment is excellent.

sentences.zh: 然李晟移軍，懷光心已惆悵，若更遣建徽、惠元就東，則使得為詞。

translations.literal: Yet Li Sheng moved the army; Huai'guang's heart is already despondent; if further Jianhui and Huiyuan are sent east, then he will obtain words as pretext.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Sheng has already moved his army, and Huai'guang is already aggrieved. If we also send Jianhui and Huiyuan east, he will have grounds for complaint.

sentences.zh: 且俟旬時。」

translations.literal: Moreover wait a ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: Let us wait a little longer.

sentences.zh: 晟至東渭橋，不旬日，懷光果奪兩節度兵，建徽單騎遁而獲免，惠元中路被執，害之。

translations.literal: Sheng reached East Wei Bridge; within ten days, Huai'guang indeed seized the two military governors' armies; Jianhui fled alone on horseback and escaped; Huiyuan was seized on the road and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng reached East Wei Bridge. Within ten days Huai'guang seized the armies of the two governors. Jianhui escaped alone on horseback; Huiyuan was captured on the road and killed.

sentences.zh: 報至行在，人情大恐。

translations.literal: The report reached the traveling court; people's hearts greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached the emperor's camp, panic seized everyone.

sentences.zh: 翌日，移幸山南。

translations.literal: The next day, the court moved in favor to Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor moved his court to Shannan.

sentences.zh: 贄練達兵機，率如此類。

translations.literal: Zhi, versed in military opportunity, was generally of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi understood military affairs with similar insight throughout.

sentences.zh: 二月，從幸梁州，轉諫議大夫，依前充學士。

translations.literal: In the second month, following the imperial progress to Liang Prefecture, he was transferred to Remonstrating Censor, continuing as before as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he accompanied the emperor to Liangzhou and was promoted to Remonstrating Censor while continuing as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 先是，鳳翔衙將李楚琳乘涇師之亂，殺節度使張鎰，歸款硃泚。

translations.literal: Before this, Fengxiang garrison general Li Chulin, taking advantage of the Jing army's disorder, killed Military Governor Zhang Yi and submitted allegiance to Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Chulin, a garrison officer at Fengxiang, had taken advantage of the disorder among the Jingzhou troops to kill the military governor Zhang Yi and declare allegiance to Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 及奉天解圍，楚琳遣使貢奉，時方艱阻，不獲已，命為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: When Fengtian's siege was lifted, Chulin sent envoys with tribute; the time was just difficult and obstructed; having no choice, he was appointed Fengxiang Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of Fengtian was lifted, Chulin sent envoys with tribute. The court, still in dire straits, had no choice but to appoint him military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 然德宗忿其弒逆，心不能容，才至漢中，欲令渾瑊代為節度。

translations.literal: Yet Dezong resented his regicide and rebellion, his heart unable to tolerate; scarcely arrived at Hanzhong, he wished to have Hun Jian replace him as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, however, could not forgive Chulin's murder and treason. As soon as he reached Hanzhong, he wanted Hun Jian to replace him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：「楚琳之罪，固不容誅，但以乘輿未復，大憝猶存，勤王之師，悉在畿內，急宣速告，晷刻是爭。

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated, saying: "Chulin's crime indeed cannot tolerate execution, but because the imperial carriage is not yet restored, the great foe still exists, the armies hastening to aid the king all within the capital region—urgent proclamation and swift report, moments and quarters are contested.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi remonstrated: "Chulin's crimes certainly deserve death. But the emperor has not yet returned to the capital, the great rebel still holds power, and all the armies that came to the throne's aid are still in the vicinity. Every moment counts in dispatching orders.

sentences.zh: 商嶺則道迂且遙，駱谷復為賊所扼，僅通王命，唯在褒斜，此路若又阻艱，南北便成隔絕。

translations.literal: Shang Ridge then route winding and also distant; Luogu again by bandits choked; barely passing royal commands lies only in Baoxie—this route if again obstructed and hard, north and south then become cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The route over the Shang Mountains is long and circuitous, and Luogu Pass is again held by the enemy. Imperial orders can barely get through only via Baoxie. If that route is also blocked, north and south will be completely cut off.

sentences.zh: 以諸鎮危疑之勢，居二逆誘脅之中，恟々群情，各懷向背。

translations.literal: With the various prefectures in perilous and doubting posture, dwelling between two rebels' enticement and coercion, clamorous crowd sentiment, each harbors turning back or facing forward.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies are uncertain and caught between two rebels who press and seduce them. Public feeling is turbulent, and each man wavers between loyalty and defection.

sentences.zh: 賊勝則往，我勝則來，其間事機，不容差跌。

translations.literal: Bandits win then they go; we win then they come—the affairs within, opportunity does not tolerate slip or fall.
translations.idiomatic: They will go over to whichever side is winning. At such a moment we cannot afford the slightest misstep.

sentences.zh: 儻楚琳發憾，公肆猖狂，南塞要沖，東延巨猾，則我咽喉梗而心膂分矣，其勢豈不病哉！」

translations.literal: If Chulin releases resentment and openly unfolds wild madness, blocking the south's vital pass, extending east to the great villain—then our throat choked and heart-and-back divided; would not the posture be afflicted!
translations.idiomatic: If Chulin turns hostile and acts recklessly, he will block the vital southern route and link up with the great rebel in the east. Our throat will be cut and our forces divided. Would that not be disastrous!

sentences.zh: 上釋然開悟，乃善待楚琳使，優詔安慰其心。

translations.literal: The emperor, relieved and opened to enlightenment, then treated Chulin's envoys well, with a favorable edict comforting his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his point and treated Chulin's envoys kindly, sending a gracious edict to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 德宗至梁，欲以谷口已北從臣賜號曰「奉天定難功臣」，谷口已南隨扈者曰「元從功臣」，不選朝官，一例俱賜。

translations.literal: Dezong reached Liang, wishing to give those who followed north of Gukou the title "Meritorious Subduer of Difficulty at Fengtian," and south of Gukou the escort title "Original Follower Meritorious Servants," not selecting court officials—all alike bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong reached Liangzhou, he proposed to grant the title "Meritorious Pacifier of the Fengtian Crisis" to followers who had been north of Gukou and "Meritorious Companion from the Outset" to those who had accompanied him south of Gukou—all without distinction between court officials and others.

sentences.zh: 贄奏曰：「破賊扞難，武臣之效。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized, saying: "Breaking bandits and defending difficulty are military ministers' achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi memorialized: "Defeating rebels and bearing hardship are the deeds of military men.

sentences.zh: 至如宮闈近侍，班列員僚，但馳走從行而已，忽與介胄奮命之士，俱號功臣，伏恐武臣憤惋。」

translations.literal: As for inner palace close attendants, ranks of staff officials—they only ran and followed the march—suddenly with armored men exerting life called meritorious servants, I humbly fear military ministers will be indignant and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants and ordinary officials merely followed along. To call them meritorious alongside soldiers who fought in armor may provoke resentment among the military.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Then he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 李晟既收京城，遣中使宣付翰林院具錄先散失宮人名字，令草詔賜渾瑊，遣於奉天尋訪，以得為限，仍量與資糧送赴行在。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, having recovered the capital, sent a palace envoy to proclaim and deliver to the Hanlin Academy a full record of the names of palace women first scattered and lost, ordering a draft edict granted to Hun Jian, sent to Fengtian to search and visit, limited by those obtained, still measuring grain and supplies to send to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Sheng recaptured the capital, he sent an imperial envoy to the Hanlin Academy with orders to compile a list of palace women who had been displaced, draft an edict for Hun Jian, and send him to Fengtian to find them and escort them to the emperor's camp with provisions.

sentences.zh: 贄不時奉詔，進狀論之曰：

translations.literal: Zhi did not promptly obey the edict, submitted a memorial discussing it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi did not draft the edict immediately. Instead he submitted a memorial arguing:

sentences.zh: 頃以理道乖錯，禍亂薦鐘，陛下思咎懼災，裕人罪己，屢降大號，誓將更新。

translations.literal: Recently because the Way of government was wrong and awry, calamity and disorder repeatedly struck the bell; Your Majesty reflected on fault and feared disaster, enlarged the people and blamed himself, repeatedly lowered great proclamations, swearing to renew.
translations.idiomatic: Because governance had gone astray, calamity followed calamity. Your Majesty reflected on his errors, blamed himself before the people, and repeatedly issued great amnesties, vowing to begin anew.

sentences.zh: 天下之人，垂涕相賀，懲忿釋怨，煦仁戴明，畢力同心，共平多難。

translations.literal: People under Heaven, tears hanging, congratulated one another; chastened anger released resentment, warmed by benevolence bearing brilliance, exhausted strength united in heart, together pacifying many difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: The people wept with joy, set aside old grievances, and united in gratitude to restore peace together.

sentences.zh: 止土崩於絕岸，收版蕩於橫流，殄寇清都，不失舊物。

translations.literal: Stopped earth collapse at sheer cliff, gathered floating boards in crosscurrent, exterminated bandits and cleared the capital, not losing old possessions.
translations.idiomatic: You halted collapse at the brink, gathered the fragments from the flood, destroyed the rebels, and recovered the capital without losing the dynasty's heritage.

sentences.zh: 實由陛下至誠動於天地，深悔感於神人，故得百靈降康，兆庶歸德。

translations.literal: Truly because Your Majesty's utmost sincerity moved Heaven and Earth, deep repentance touched spirits and men, therefore obtained the hundred spirits descending with peace, the myriad masses returning to virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Your Majesty's sincerity moved Heaven and Earth and your repentance touched gods and men, so that all spirits brought peace and the people returned to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 茍不如此，自古何嘗有捐棄宮闕，失守宗祧，繼逆於赴難之師，再遷於蒙塵之日，不逾半歲，而復興大業者乎！

translations.literal: If not so, from antiquity when has there been abandoning palace halls, losing ancestral temple, rebel armies succeeding relief armies, twice moving on days of dust-covered robes—not exceeding half a year yet reviving the great enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Without this, when in all history has an emperor who abandoned his palace, lost his ancestral shrine, faced successive rebellions while rallying relief armies, and fled twice in disgrace restored the empire in less than half a year?

sentences.zh: 今渠魁始平，法駕將返，近自郊甸，遠周寰瀛，百役疲瘵之氓，重戰傷殘之卒，皆忍死扶病，傾耳聳肩，想聞德聲，翹望聖澤。

translations.literal: Now the ringleader just pacified, the imperial carriage about to return, near from suburban fields, far circling all within the seas—the hundred corvée-weary sick commoners, repeatedly battle-wounded maimed soldiers, all enduring death and supporting illness, inclining ears and raising shoulders, thinking to hear virtue's voice, craning to hope for sage grace.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the rebel leader has just been crushed and the imperial carriage is about to return, from the capital outskirts to the farthest corners of the realm, exhausted laborers and battle-wounded soldiers alike endure their pain, straining to hear your benevolent words and hoping for your grace.

sentences.zh: 陛下固當感上天悔禍之眷，荷列祖垂裕之休，念將士鋒刃之殃，湣黎元塗炭之酷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should indeed feel Heaven's repentant calamity-favoring regard, bear the former emperors' overflowing surplus of blessing, recall the soldiers' blade calamity, pity the common people's charcoal-smeared cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should respond to Heaven's mercy in turning aside disaster, honor the blessing left by your ancestors, remember the wounds of your soldiers, and pity the suffering of the people.

sentences.zh: 以致寇為戒，以居上為危，以務理為憂，以復宮為急。

translations.literal: Take inviting bandits as warning, occupying the heights as peril, striving for order as worry, restoring the palace as urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Take the rebels as a warning, regard your position as perilous, make good governance your concern, and return to the palace your urgent task.

sentences.zh: 損之又損，尚懼汰侈之易滋；

translations.literal: Reduce again and again, still fearing extravagant excess easily spreading.
translations.idiomatic: You must keep stripping away excess, for luxury spreads easily.

sentences.zh: 艱之惟艱，猶患戒慎之難久。

translations.literal: Hard it is and only hard, still worrying vigilance and caution hard to last long.
translations.idiomatic: The road ahead is hard, and vigilance is hard to sustain.

sentences.zh: 謀始盡善，克終已稀；

translations.literal: Planning the start with utmost goodness, completing the end is already rare.
translations.idiomatic: Many begin well.

sentences.zh: 始而不謀，終則何有！

translations.literal: Start without planning, end then what is there!
translations.idiomatic: Few finish well. If you do not plan from the beginning, what can you hope for at the end?

sentences.zh: 夫以內人為號，蓋是中壺末流。

translations.literal: As for using palace women as the call, this is the inner quarters' lowest stream.
translations.idiomatic: To make palace women the priority belongs to the least worthy concerns of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 天子之尊，富有宮掖，如此等輩，固繁有徒，但恐傷多，豈憂乏使！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's eminence richly possesses palace inner quarters; such as these indeed abound in multitudes—only fear hurting too many, how worry lacking servants!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has a full palace. Such women are hardly scarce. You should fear causing too much harm, not worry about finding attendants!

sentences.zh: 翦除元惡，曾未浹辰，奔賀往來，道途如織。

translations.literal: Cutting away the origin villain, not yet ten days wet; rushing congratulations coming and going, roads like weaving.
translations.idiomatic: The chief villain has been eliminated only days ago. Messengers of congratulation fill the roads like threads on a loom.

sentences.zh: 何必自虧君德，首訪婦人，又令資裝速赴行在！

translations.literal: Why must you yourself diminish lordly virtue, first visiting women, again ordering supplies and dress swiftly sent to the traveling court!
translations.idiomatic: Why diminish your stature as ruler by seeking out women first and ordering them rushed to your camp with provisions?

sentences.zh: 萬目閱視，眾口流傳，恐非所以答慶賴之心，副惟新之望也。

translations.literal: Ten thousand eyes watch and see, crowd mouths spread word—I fear this is not the means to answer celebratory reliance's hearts or fulfill renewal's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand eyes are watching and ten thousand tongues are speaking. This will not meet the people's joy and hope for renewal.

sentences.zh: 夫事有先後，義有重輕，重者宜先，輕者宜後。

translations.literal: Affairs have before and after, principle has heavy and light—heavy should be first, light should be after.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs have their order of priority. Weighty matters come first; lesser ones afterward.

sentences.zh: 武王克殷，有未及下車而為之者，有下車而為之者，蓋美其不失先後之宜也。

translations.literal: King Wu conquered Yin; some things not yet reached dismounting the chariot he did, some after dismounting—praising that he did not lose the fitting order of before and after.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu conquered the Shang, some things he did before he even left his chariot and others only after he dismounted—because he never lost the proper sense of priority.

sentences.zh: 自翠華播越，萬姓靡依，清廟震驚，三時乏祀，當今所務，莫大於斯。

translations.literal: Since the azure carriage scattered and crossed, myriad people had none to rely on; the clear temple was shaken and alarmed, three seasons lacked sacrifice—today's affairs, nothing greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial progress fled into exile, the people have been without refuge, the ancestral temple has been desecrated, and sacrifices have ceased for seasons. Nothing is more urgent than this.

sentences.zh: 誠宜速遣大臣，馳傳先往，迎復神主，修整郊壇，展禋享之儀，申告謝之意。

translations.literal: Truly fitting to swiftly dispatch great ministers, post-horses speeding ahead, welcome and restore the spirit tablets, repair suburban altars, unfold sacrifice and offering rites, declare gratitude and apology's intent.
translations.idiomatic: You should promptly send high ministers posthaste to recover the spirit tablets of the ancestors, restore the suburban altars, perform the sacrificial rites, and offer thanks to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 然後吊恤死義，慰犒有功，綏輯黎蒸，優問耆耋。

translations.literal: Then condole and comfort those who died in righteousness, comfort and reward those with merit, pacify and gather the common masses, graciously inquire of the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Then mourn the dead, reward the meritorious, restore order among the people, and show kindness to the elderly.

sentences.zh: 安定反側，寬宥脅從；

translations.literal: Stabilize the wavering, pardon the coerced followers.
translations.idiomatic: Reassure those who wavered and pardon those who were forced to follow the rebels.

sentences.zh: 宣暢郁堙，褒獎忠直；

translations.literal: Proclaim and clear what was pent and blocked, praise and reward the loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Give voice to silenced grievances and honor the loyal and upright.

sentences.zh: 官失職之士，復廢業之人。

translations.literal: Officials who lost their posts, people who resumed abandoned livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Restore officials who lost their posts and help those whose livelihoods were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 是皆宜先，不可後也。

translations.literal: These all should be first, cannot be after.
translations.idiomatic: All of these should come first, not last.

sentences.zh: 至如崇飾服器，繕緝殿臺，備耳目之娛，選巾櫛之侍，是皆宜後，不可先也。

translations.literal: As for honoring and adorning garments and vessels, repairing and joining halls and terraces, preparing eye-and-ear pleasure, selecting towel-and-comb attendants—these all should be after, cannot be first.
translations.idiomatic: As for fine dress and ornaments, palace repairs, diversions for amusement, and choosing personal attendants—these must wait and cannot come first.

sentences.zh: 散失內人，已經累月，既當離亂之際，必為將士所私。

translations.literal: Scattered and lost palace women have already piled up months; having been at separation and disorder's moment, they must have been privately taken by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The displaced palace women have been gone for months. In the chaos they have surely been taken by soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其人若稍有知，不求當自陳獻；

translations.literal: If the person slightly has understanding, without seeking she will naturally declare and present herself.
translations.idiomatic: If any are sensible, they will come forward on their own without being sought.

sentences.zh: 其人若甚無識，求之適使憂虞。

translations.literal: If the person is very without understanding, seeking them only makes worry and anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: If any are foolish, searching for them will only cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 自因寇亂喪亡，頗有大於此者，一聞搜索，懷懼必多；

translations.literal: Since because of bandit disorder there are losses and deaths, quite many greater than this—once hearing search, harboring fear must be many.
translations.idiomatic: Many have suffered losses far worse in the rebellion. Once a search is announced, fear will spread widely.

sentences.zh: 余孽尚繁，群情未一，因而善撫，猶恐危疑，若又懼之，於何不有！

translations.literal: Remaining spawn still numerous, crowd sentiment not one—thereby well comforting, still fearing peril and doubt; if again feared, what would not exist!
translations.idiomatic: Rebel remnants are still numerous and public feeling is not yet unified. Even with gentle handling they remain unsettled. If you frighten them further, what calamity might not follow?

sentences.zh: 昔人所以掩絕纓而飲盜馬者，豈必忘其情愛，蓋知為君之體然也。

translations.literal: The ancients therefore covered the dropped cap cord and drank of the stolen horse—not that they must forget their affection, but knew the bearing of a lord is thus.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients who hid a dropped cap-string and watered a stolen horse did not forget personal attachment. They understood what conduct befits a ruler.

sentences.zh: 以小妨大，明者不為。

translations.literal: Using small to obstruct great—clear-minded men do not do this.
translations.idiomatic: The wise do not let small matters obstruct great ones.

sentences.zh: 天下固多褻人，何必獨在於此。

translations.literal: Under Heaven indeed has many immodest people—why must it be only among these?
translations.idiomatic: The world has no shortage of humble women. Why must you focus on these alone?

sentences.zh: 所令撰賜渾瑊詔書，未敢順旨。

translations.literal: The ordered draft edict granted to Hun Jian—your servant does not dare follow the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant dare not draft the edict for Hun Jian as ordered.

sentences.zh: 帝遂不降詔，但遣使而已。

translations.literal: The emperor then did not lower the edict, only sent envoys, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not issue the edict, and sent only an ordinary envoy.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京，轉中書舍人，學士如故。

translations.literal: Dezong returned to the capital, transferred to Secretariat Drafter, Academician as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to the capital, Lu Zhi was promoted to Secretariat Drafter while continuing as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 初，贄受張鎰知，得居內職；

translations.literal: At first, Zhi received Zhang Yi's recognition and obtained residence in inner office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu Zhi had owed his position in the inner court to Zhang Yi's patronage.

sentences.zh: 及鎰為盧杞所排，贄常憂惴；

translations.literal: When Yi was displaced by Lu Qi, Zhi often worried and feared.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yi was ousted by Lu Qi, Lu Zhi lived in constant apprehension.

sentences.zh: 及杞貶黜，始敢上書言事。

translations.literal: When Qi was demoted and dismissed, then he dared submit memorials on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Lu Qi was demoted did he dare to speak frankly in memorials.

sentences.zh: 德宗好文，益深顧遇。

translations.literal: Dezong loved literature, increasingly deep in regard and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong loved literature and favored Lu Zhi all the more.

sentences.zh: 奉天解圍後，德宗言及違離宗廟，嗚咽流涕曰：「致寇之由，實朕之過。」

translations.literal: After Fengtian's siege was lifted, Dezong speaking of departing from the ancestral temple, sobbed with flowing tears, saying: "The cause of inviting bandits is truly Our fault.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of Fengtian was lifted, Dezong spoke of having been driven from the ancestral temple and wept: "The blame for bringing on the rebels is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 贄亦流涕而對曰：「臣思致今日之患者，群臣之罪也。」

translations.literal: Zhi also flowed tears and replied, saying: "Your servant thinks those causing today's affliction are the fault of the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi wept in reply: "Your servant believes today's disaster is the fault of your ministers.

sentences.zh: 贄意蓋為盧杞、趙贊等也。

translations.literal: Zhi's meaning covered Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He had Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and others in mind.

sentences.zh: 上欲掩杞之失，則曰：「雖朕德薄，致茲禍亂，亦運數前定，事不由人。」

translations.literal: The emperor wishing to cover Qi's fault, then said: "Though Our virtue is thin, causing this calamity and disorder, also fate's number was pre-fixed—affairs not by men's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to shield Lu Qi, the emperor said: "Though my virtue is insufficient and brought this calamity, it was also fated—beyond human control.

sentences.zh: 贄又極言杞等罪狀，上雖貌從，心頗不說。

translations.literal: Zhi again exhaustively spoke Qi's and the others' crimes; the emperor though in appearance assented, in heart quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi again enumerated the crimes of Lu Qi and the others. The emperor seemed to agree but was inwardly displeased.

sentences.zh: 吳通微兄弟俱在翰林，亦承德宗寵遇，文章才器不迨贄；

translations.literal: Wu Tongwei's brothers were both in the Hanlin, also receiving Dezong's favor; literary composition and talent fell short of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tongwei and his brothers served in the Hanlin and also enjoyed Dezong's favor, though their literary talent did not match Lu Zhi's.

sentences.zh: 而能交結權幸，共短贄於上前。

translations.literal: Yet able to connect with powerful favorites, together slandering Zhi before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: But they cultivated connections with the powerful and slandered Lu Zhi before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 故劉從一、姜公輔自卑品蒼黃之中，皆登輔相；

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu from low rank in the pale yellow middle all ascended to chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu rose from humble posts amid the crisis to become chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 而贄為朋黨所擠，同職害其能，加以言事激切，動失上之歡心，故久之不為輔相。

translations.literal: Yet Zhi was squeezed by faction parties, colleagues harmed by his ability, adding memorials on affairs intensely cutting, often losing the emperor's pleased heart—therefore long not made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, squeezed out by faction and envied by colleagues, and because his memorials were blunt and often displeased the emperor, was long passed over for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 其於議論應對，明練理體，敷陳剖判，下筆如神，當時名流，無不推挹。

translations.literal: In discussion and response, clear and practiced in principle's substance, laying out and dissecting judgments, putting brush to paper like a spirit; the leading figures of the time—none did not esteem and defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: In debate and reply he grasped principle with luminous clarity, unfolding arguments with penetrating analysis and writing as if divinely inspired. Every eminent man of the age held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，李抱真入朝，從容奏曰：「陛下幸奉天、山南時，赦書至山東，宣諭之時，士卒無不感泣。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenyuan era, Li Baozhen entered court and, at ease, memorialized, saying: "When Your Majesty arrived at Fengtian and Shan'nan, the amnesty edict reached Shandong; at the time of proclamation and instruction, the soldiers none failed to feel moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era, Li Baozhen came to court and said calmly to the emperor: "When Your Majesty took refuge at Fengtian and in the south, the amnesty edict reached Shandong. When it was read aloud, not a soldier failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 臣即時見人情如此，知賊不足平也。」

translations.literal: Your servant at once saw human sentiment thus and knew the rebels were insufficient to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: I saw the people's hearts at once and knew the rebels could not be easily crushed."

sentences.zh: 時贄母韋氏在江東，上遣中使迎至京師，搢紳榮之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhi's mother the Lady Wei was in Jiangdong; the emperor sent a palace envoy to welcome her to the capital—the gentry honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi's mother, Lady Wei, was then in Jiangdong. The emperor sent a palace envoy to bring her to the capital, to the admiration of the court.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂，東歸洛陽，寓居嵩山豐樂寺。

translations.literal: Soon he encountered his mother's bereavement, returned east to Luoyang, and lodged at Fengle Temple on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother, returned east to Luoyang, and took lodging at Fengle Temple on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 籓鎮賻贈及別陳餉遺，一無所取。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts from the fief commanders and separately presented offerings—he took none of them.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of the condolence gifts sent by regional commanders or the private offerings they pressed upon him.

sentences.zh: 與韋臯布衣時相善，唯西川致遺，奏而受之。

translations.literal: With Wei Gao he had been close in commoner days; only from Xichuan did Gao send gifts—these Zhi memorialized about and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wei Gao had been friends since their days as commoners. Only gifts from Wei in the west were accepted—and then only after Lu Zhi had memorialized the court and received permission.

sentences.zh: 贄父初葬蘇州，至是欲合葬。

translations.literal: Zhi's father had first been buried in Suzhou; at this time he wished a joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: His father had first been buried in Suzhou; Lu Zhi now wished to move the grave for a joint burial with his mother.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使護其柩車至洛，其禮遇如此。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to escort the coffin carriage to Luoyang—the courtesy treatment was such.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to escort the coffin to Luoyang—a mark of the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 免喪，權知兵部侍郎，依前充學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was acting Vice Minister of War and continued as before as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed acting Vice Minister of War while retaining his post as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 申謝日，贄伏地而泣，德宗為之改容敘慰。

translations.literal: On the day of presenting thanks, Zhi prostrated himself and wept; Dezong because of this changed expression and comforted him with words.
translations.idiomatic: When he presented his thanks, Lu Zhi prostrated himself and wept. Dezong's expression softened and he spoke to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 恩遇既隆，中外屬意為輔弼，而宰相竇參素忌贄，贄亦短參之所為，言參黷貨，由是與參不平。

translations.literal: Favor having already been lofty, inside and outside looked to him as chief minister—but the chief minister Dou Can had long been jealous of Zhi; Zhi also criticized Can's conduct, saying Can took bribes; from this he and Can were not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: With favor so high, the court expected him to become chief minister. But Chief Minister Dou Can had long resented him, and Lu Zhi in turn attacked Dou's conduct, accusing him of corrupt gain. From that point the two were at odds.

sentences.zh: 七年，罷學士，正拜兵部侍郎，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was removed as academician, formally appointed Vice Minister of War, and put in charge of the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he left the Hanlin Academy, was formally appointed Vice Minister of War, and put in charge of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 時崔元翰、梁肅文藝冠時，贄輸心於肅。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yuanhan and Liang Su's literary art crowned the age; Zhi poured his heart into Su.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan and Liang Su were then the leading literary figures of the age, and Lu Zhi put his full trust in Liang Su.

sentences.zh: 肅與元翰推薦藝實之士，升第之日，雖眾望不愜，然一歲選士，才十四五，數年之內，居臺省清近者十余人。

translations.literal: Su and Yuanhan recommended men of real literary talent; on the day ranks were conferred, though general expectation was not satisfied, yet in one year's selection of scholars there were only fourteen or fifteen; within several years, more than ten held clean and close posts in the Board and Department offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Su and Cui Yuanhan recommended men of genuine talent. When the successful candidates were announced, public opinion was not wholly satisfied—yet in a single year's selection only fourteen or fifteen passed, and within a few years more than ten held prestigious posts in the central boards and departments.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，竇參得罪，以贄為中書侍郎、門下同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year Dou Can incurred guilt; Zhi was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor with the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year Dou Can fell from power, and Lu Zhi was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 贄久為邪黨所擠，困而得位，意在不負恩獎，悉心報國，以天下事為己任。

translations.literal: Zhi, long squeezed by evil factions, gaining the post through hardship—his intent was not to fail favor and reward, to devote his heart to repaying the state, and to take affairs under Heaven as his own burden.
translations.idiomatic: Long blocked by faction, Lu Zhi had at last won the post through hardship. He meant to repay the emperor's kindness, devote himself to the state, and take the affairs of the empire as his own responsibility.

sentences.zh: 上即位之初，用楊炎、盧杞秉政，樹立朋黨，排擯良善，卒致天下沸騰，鑾輿奔播。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the emperor's accession, employing Yang Yan and Lu Qi to hold government, establishing faction cliques, excluding and driving out the good—finally causing all under Heaven to boil and the imperial carriage to flee and wander.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign the emperor had put Yang Yan and Lu Qi in power. They built factions, drove out the worthy, and in the end threw the realm into turmoil and forced the emperor himself into flight.

sentences.zh: 懲是之失，貞元已後，雖立輔臣，至於小官除擬，上必再三詳問，久之方下。

translations.literal: Penalizing this failure, after the Zhenyuan era even when chief ministers were appointed, as for minor offices' appointments and nominations the emperor necessarily questioned repeatedly in detail; only after a long time were orders issued.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by that failure, after the Zhenyuan era the emperor, even after appointing chief ministers, would repeatedly question every minor appointment in detail and delay issuing orders for a long time.

sentences.zh: 及贄知政事，請許臺省長官自薦屬官，仍保任之，事有曠敗，兼坐舉主。
