translations.literal: When Zhi managed state affairs, he requested permission for Board and Department chiefs to recommend their own subordinate officials and still guarantee them; if affairs had negligence and failure, the recommender was jointly implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi took charge of government, he asked that heads of the central boards and departments be allowed to recommend their own subordinates and guarantee their conduct, with the recommender held jointly liable if a nominee failed in office.

sentences.zh: 上許之，俄又宣旨曰：「外議云：『諸司所舉，多引用親黨，兼通賂遺，不得實才。』

translations.literal: The emperor assented; soon again issued an edict, saying: "Outside discussion says: 'What the various offices recommend mostly employs kin and faction, together with passing bribes and gifts—not obtaining real talent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, but soon issued another edict: "Outside opinion says the offices mostly recommend relatives and allies, pass bribes, and fail to produce truly capable men.

sentences.zh: 此法行之非便，今後卿等宜自選擇，勿用諸司延薦。」

translations.literal: This method carried out is not convenient; hereafter you ministers should yourselves select—do not use the various offices' extended recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: This policy is awkward in practice. Hereafter you ministers should choose men yourselves and not rely on recommendations from the offices.

sentences.zh: 贄論奏曰：

translations.literal: Zhi argued in memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi submitted a reasoned memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣實頑鄙，一無所堪，猥蒙任使，待罪宰相。

translations.literal: Your servant is truly obstinate and base, capable in nothing, undeservedly receiving appointment, awaiting punishment as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is truly dull and unworthy, fit for nothing, yet undeservedly raised to the chancellorship to serve at risk of fault.

sentences.zh: 雖懷竊位之懼，且乏知人之明，自揣庸虛，終難上報。

translations.literal: Though harboring fear of usurping the post, and moreover lacking the clarity to know men, measuring myself common and empty, in the end I can hardly repay above.
translations.idiomatic: Though I fear I hold a post beyond my desert, and though I lack the discernment to know men well, I know myself to be mediocre and can scarcely hope to repay Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 唯知廣求才之路，使賢者各以匯征；

translations.literal: I know only to broaden the road of seeking talent, causing worthy men each to be gathered in summons.
translations.idiomatic: I know only that the path to talent must be widened so that the worthy may each be summoned forth together.

sentences.zh: 啟至公之門，令職司皆得自達。

translations.literal: Open the gate of utmost fairness, causing every office to be able to reach self-expression.
translations.idiomatic: Open the gate of perfect fairness so that every office may make itself known.

sentences.zh: 既蒙允許，即宜宣行。

translations.literal: Having received permission, it then ought to be proclaimed and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Having received Your Majesty's approval, the policy ought at once to be proclaimed and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 南宮舉人，才至十數，或非臺省舊吏，則是使府佐僚，累經薦延，多歷事任。

translations.literal: Southern Palace examination candidates were only ten-odd in number; some were not old clerks of the Boards and Departments, then they were staff of commissioner offices, repeatedly recommended and extended, many having passed through duties and posts.
translations.idiomatic: The recent examination passers numbered only a dozen or so. Some were not former clerks of the central boards and departments but staff of commissioner offices, repeatedly recommended and long experienced in office.

sentences.zh: 論其資望，既不愧於班行；

translations.literal: Speaking of their qualifications and standing, they already did not fail to match their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In seniority and reputation they were fit for their ranks.

sentences.zh: 考其行能，又未聞於闕敗。

translations.literal: Examining their conduct and ability, again none were heard of in neglect and failure.
translations.idiomatic: In conduct and ability none had yet been found deficient.

sentences.zh: 遽以騰口，上煩聖聰，道之難行，亦可知矣！

translations.literal: Abruptly because of clamoring mouths, above troubling sage hearing—the Way's difficulty in practice also can be known!
translations.idiomatic: Yet at once the mouths of rumor stir, troubling Your Majesty's ear. How difficult it is to put sound policy into practice is plain enough!

sentences.zh: 陛下勤求理道，務徇物情，因謂舉薦非宜，復委宰臣揀擇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty diligently seeks the Way of order, striving to follow the people's sentiment; therefore you say recommendation is not fitting and again entrust chief ministers to select and choose.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty earnestly seeks good government and attends to public feeling, and for that reason you hold that recommendation is unsuitable and again leave selection to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 其為崇任輔弼，博采輿詞，可謂聖德之盛者。

translations.literal: This in reverencing and trusting chief ministers and broadly gathering public discourse can be called overflowing sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In honoring your ministers and heeding public opinion, this shows the greatness of your sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 然於委任責成之道，聽言考實之方，閑邪存誠，猶恐有闕。

translations.literal: Yet in the Way of entrusting responsibility and demanding fulfillment, the method of listening to words and examining reality, restraining evil and preserving sincerity—still I fear there are gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in entrusting responsibility, testing speech against fact, and keeping out evil while holding to sincerity, I fear something is still lacking.

sentences.zh: 陛下既納臣言而用之，旋聞橫議而止之，於臣謀不責成，於橫議不考實，此乃謀失者得以辭其罪，議曲者得以肆其誣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty having accepted your servant's words and used them, soon hearing perverse discussion and stopping them—toward your servant's plans not demanding fulfillment, toward perverse discussion not examining reality—this is whereby those whose plans fail can use words to excuse their guilt, and those whose discussion is crooked can freely spread their slander.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty accepted my proposal and put it into effect, then at once halted it on hearing reckless criticism. You hold me to no account for the plan's failure, yet you do not test the reckless critics' claims. Thus those whose counsel fails may excuse their fault, and those who speak crookedly may slander at will.

sentences.zh: 率是而行，觸類而長，固無必定之計，亦無必實之言。

translations.literal: Following this as model and acting, touching each category it grows—indeed no fixed and certain plans, also no necessarily true words.
translations.idiomatic: If this pattern continues and spreads by analogy, there will be no settled policy and no speech that can be trusted as true.

sentences.zh: 計不定則理道難成，言不實則小人得誌。

translations.literal: Plans not fixed then the Way of order is hard to complete; words not true then petty men obtain their wish.
translations.idiomatic: Without settled plans good government cannot be achieved; without truthful speech petty men get their way.

sentences.zh: 國家之病，常必由之。

translations.literal: The state's illness constantly must proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: The state's afflictions commonly spring from this.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公問管仲害霸之事，對曰：「得賢不能任，害霸也；

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong what harmed hegemony; he answered: "Getting worthy men yet unable to employ them—harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong what harmed hegemony. He answered: "To gain worthy men yet fail to employ them harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 用而不能終，害霸也；

translations.literal: To employ them yet be unable to see them through—harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: To employ them yet fail to see the appointment through harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 與賢人謀事，而與小人議之，害霸也。」

translations.literal: To consult with worthy men on affairs yet discuss them with petty men—harms hegemony."
translations.idiomatic: To plan with worthy men yet debate the plan with petty men harms hegemony."

sentences.zh: 為小人者，不必悉懷險诐，故覆邦家。

translations.literal: Petty men do not necessarily all harbor treacherous deceit, thus overturning state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men need not all harbor treacherous intent in order to ruin state and family.

sentences.zh: 蓋以其意性回邪，趣向狹促，以沮議為出眾，以自異為不群，趨近利而昧遠圖，效小信而傷大道，況又言行難保，恣其非心者乎！

translations.literal: For their minds and natures are twisted and perverse, their bent narrow and cramped—they take obstructing deliberation as standing out, taking themselves as different as not joining the group, rushing toward near profit while blind to far design, imitating small trustworthiness while harming the great Way—how much more when words and conduct are hard to guarantee and they indulge their wicked hearts!
translations.idiomatic: Their minds are crooked and their outlook cramped. They treat obstruction as distinction, eccentricity as independence, near gain as wisdom and far design as folly, small shows of trustworthiness as virtue and the great Way as expendable—and all the more so when their words and deeds cannot be trusted and they indulge their private malice!

sentences.zh: 伏以宰輔，常制不過數人，人之所知，固有限極，不有遍諳諸士，備閱群才。

translations.literal: I submit that chief ministers, by regular rule no more than several men—what men know indeed has a bounded limit; they do not everywhere know all scholars or completely review all talent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers, by custom, number only a few. What any man can know is necessarily limited; they cannot know every scholar or review every talent in the realm.

sentences.zh: 若令悉命群官，理須展轉詢訪，是則變公舉為私薦，易明易攵為暗投。

translations.literal: If ordered to command all officials, by principle they must extend and turn in inquiry and investigation—then this changes public recommendation to private recommendation, open recommendation to secret recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: If the chief ministers must appoint every official themselves, they can only do so by making round after round of private inquiry—turning public recommendation into private patronage and open selection into back-room nomination.

sentences.zh: 儻如議者之言，所舉多有情故，舉於君上，且未絕私；

translations.literal: If like the discussants' words, what is recommended mostly has personal ties; recommending to the lord above, still private favor is not ended;
translations.idiomatic: If the critics are right that recommendations are mostly made through personal ties, then even when names are sent to Your Majesty private favor is not eliminated;

sentences.zh: 薦於宰臣，安肯無詐！

translations.literal: Recommending to chief ministers—how can there fail to be fraud!
translations.idiomatic: when names are sent to the chief ministers, how can fraud be avoided!

sentences.zh: 失人之弊，必又甚焉。

translations.literal: The harm of losing good men must again be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: The loss of capable men will be even worse.

sentences.zh: 所以承前命官，罕有不涉私謗，雖則秉鈞不一，或自行情，亦由私訪所親，轉為所賣。

translations.literal: Therefore formerly in appointing officials, rarely were there not entanglements of private slander; though holding the scale not uniform, some acted by personal feeling—also because private inquiries to kin were in turn sold out by them.
translations.idiomatic: That is why past appointments were rarely free of private complaint. Even when chief ministers differed in judgment and some acted from personal inclination, they still relied on private inquiries among their intimates—and were in turn betrayed by them.

sentences.zh: 其弊非遠，聖鑒明知。

translations.literal: This harm is not distant; sage discernment clearly knows it.
translations.idiomatic: This evil is not remote; Your Majesty knows it well.

sentences.zh: 今又將徇浮言，專任宰臣除吏，宰臣不遍諳識，踵前須訪於人。

translations.literal: Now again about to follow floating words, exclusively entrusting chief ministers to remove and appoint officials—chief ministers do not everywhere know and recognize, and following precedent must inquire of others.
translations.idiomatic: Now, yielding again to loose talk, you would leave appointment entirely to the chief ministers. They cannot know everyone themselves and, as before, must ask others.

sentences.zh: 若訪親朋，則是悔其覆車，不易故轍；

translations.literal: If inquiring of kin and friends, then this regrets the overturned cart and does not change the old rut;
translations.idiomatic: If they ask kin and friends, they repeat the old mistake and change nothing;

sentences.zh: 若訪於朝列，則是求其私薦，不如公舉之愈也。

translations.literal: If inquiring among the court ranks, then this seeks their private recommendations—not as good as public recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: if they ask colleagues at court, they solicit private recommendations—which is no better than open recommendation.

sentences.zh: 二者利害，惟陛下更詳擇焉。

translations.literal: Of the two, benefit and harm—may Your Majesty further examine and choose.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two courses, may Your Majesty weigh the benefit and harm.

sentences.zh: 恐不如委任長官，慎揀僚屬，所揀既少，所求亦精，得賢有鑒識之名，失實當暗謬之責。

translations.literal: I fear it is not as good as entrusting department chiefs, carefully selecting subordinates—those selected being few, what is sought also refined; gaining worthy men brings a name for discernment, losing on reality ought to bear the blame of hidden error.
translations.idiomatic: Better, I fear, to entrust department chiefs to choose their subordinates carefully. Fewer men would be chosen, but the search would be sharper. Success would bring them credit for discernment; failure would bring blame for error.

sentences.zh: 人之常性，莫不愛身，況於臺省長官，皆是當朝華選，孰肯徇私妄舉，以傷名取責者耶！

translations.literal: Men's constant nature—none do not love their bodies; how much more for Board and Department chiefs, all being the dynasty's splendid selections—who would willingly favor private ties and rashly recommend, to harm their name and invite blame!
translations.idiomatic: Human nature being what it is, every man protects his own reputation—how much more the heads of the central boards and departments, all chosen from the finest of the court. Who among them would risk his name by recommending unworthy men for private reasons!

sentences.zh: 所謂臺省長官，即僕射、尚書、左右丞、侍郎及御史大夫、中丞是也。

translations.literal: What are called Board and Department chiefs are precisely the Grand Masters, Ministers, Left and Right Vice Directors, Vice Ministers, and the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: By Board and Department chiefs I mean the Grandees, Ministers, Left and Right Vice Directors, Vice Ministers, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 陛下比擇輔相，多亦出於其中。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in recent selection of chief ministers—many also came from among them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the chief ministers Your Majesty has lately chosen came from among them.

sentences.zh: 今之宰臣，則往日臺省長官也；

translations.literal: Today's chief ministers are then the former Board and Department chiefs;
translations.idiomatic: Today's chief ministers were yesterday's board and department heads;

sentences.zh: 今之臺省長官，乃將來之宰臣也，但是職名暫異，固非行業頓殊。

translations.literal: Today's Board and Department chiefs are the future chief ministers; only the office names are temporarily different—not at all that conduct and calling are suddenly separate.
translations.idiomatic: and today's board and department heads are tomorrow's chief ministers. Only the titles differ for a time; their character and capacity are not suddenly transformed.

sentences.zh: 豈有為長官之時不能舉一二屬吏，居宰臣之位則可擇千百具僚，物議悠悠，其惑斯甚。

translations.literal: How can it be that when serving as department chief one cannot recommend one or two subordinate clerks, yet occupying the chief minister's place one can choose hundreds and thousands of officials—public discussion endless, how very confusing!
translations.idiomatic: How can the same men who, as department heads, could not be trusted to recommend one or two subordinates suddenly, as chief ministers, be expected to choose hundreds and thousands of officials? Public opinion is baffled indeed.

sentences.zh: 夫求才貴廣，考課貴精。

translations.literal: Seeking talent values breadth; examining performance values precision.
translations.idiomatic: In seeking talent breadth matters; in judging performance precision matters.

sentences.zh: 求廣在於各舉所知，長吏之薦擇是也；

translations.literal: Breadth in seeking lies in each recommending what one knows—the department chiefs' recommendations and selections are this;
translations.idiomatic: Breadth lies in each man recommending those he knows—the department chiefs' selections serve this purpose;

sentences.zh: 貴精在於按名責實，宰臣之序進是也。

translations.literal: Precision in valuation lies in matching names to reality and demanding results—the chief ministers' ordered advancement is this.
translations.idiomatic: precision lies in matching names to reality and holding men accountable—the chief ministers' review serves this purpose.

sentences.zh: 往者則天太后踐祚臨朝，欲收人心，尤務拔擢，弘委任之意，開汲引之門，進用不疑，求訪無倦，非但人得薦士，亦許自舉其才。

translations.literal: Formerly Empress Wu Zetian ascended the throne and presided over court, wishing to win hearts, especially striving at promotion, broadening the intent of entrustment, opening the gate of drawing up—advancing employments without doubt, seeking and inquiring without weariness—not only could people recommend scholars, they were also permitted to recommend their own talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu Zetian came to the throne she sought to win hearts and made promotion her chief task. She opened wide the gate of appointment, advanced men without hesitation, and searched tirelessly. Not only could officials recommend others; they might even recommend themselves.

sentences.zh: 所薦必行，所舉輒試，其於選士之道，豈不傷於容易哉！

translations.literal: What was recommended must be carried out, what was nominated was immediately tested—in the Way of selecting scholars, was this not harmed by being too easy!
translations.idiomatic: Every recommendation was acted on and every nominee promptly tested. By the standards of selecting scholars, was this not dangerously easy!

sentences.zh: 而課責既嚴，進退皆速，不肖者旋黜，才能者驟升，是以當代謂知人之明，累朝賴多士之用。

translations.literal: Yet examination and responsibility being strict, advancement and removal all swift—the unworthy were quickly dismissed, the capable suddenly promoted; therefore the age was called to have clarity in knowing men, and successive courts relied on many scholars' employment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because examination was strict and promotion and dismissal swift, the unworthy were quickly removed and the capable rapidly advanced. The age was praised for knowing men, and later reigns benefited from the abundance of talent.

sentences.zh: 此乃近於求才貴廣，考課貴精之效也。

translations.literal: This is nearly the effect of seeking talent valuing breadth and examining performance valuing precision.
translations.idiomatic: This was nearly the perfect balance of breadth in seeking talent and precision in judging performance.

sentences.zh: 陛下誕膺寶歷，思致理平，雖好賢之心，有逾於前哲，而得人之盛，未迨於往時。

translations.literal: Your Majesty born to receive the precious succession, thinking to achieve order and peace—though the heart loving the worthy exceeds former sages, the flourishing of obtaining men has not reached past times.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, born to the throne and intent on bringing order, loves worthy men even more than the sages of old—yet the harvest of talent has not matched earlier times.

sentences.zh: 蓋由賞鑒獨任於聖聰，搜擇頗難於公舉，仍啟登延之路，罕施練核之方。

translations.literal: Covering because appraisal rested solely in sage discernment, searching and selection quite difficult through public recommendation, still opening the road of summoning and extending, rarely applying the method of thorough examination.
translations.idiomatic: This is because judgment rests solely with Your Majesty, open recommendation is difficult, the gate of appointment remains open, and rigorous testing is rarely applied.

sentences.zh: 遂使先進者漸益雕訛，後來者不相接續，施一令則謗沮互起，用一人則瘡磐立成。

translations.literal: Therefore causing the advanced gradually to grow more corroded and erroneous, the later comers not connecting in succession—issuing one decree then slander and obstruction rise together, employing one man then scars immediately form.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that senior men grow ever more compromised, successors fail to follow them, every decree provokes a chorus of slander, and every appointment leaves fresh scars.

sentences.zh: 此乃失於選才太精，制法不一之患也。

translations.literal: This is the affliction of failing through selecting talent too precisely and making law not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: This is the harm of selecting talent too narrowly and keeping policy unsettled.

sentences.zh: 則天舉用之法，傷易而得人；

translations.literal: Empress Wu's method of recommending and employing harmed by ease yet obtained men;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's method erred on the side of ease, yet she obtained men;

sentences.zh: 陛下慎揀之規，太精而失士。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's rule of careful selection—too precise and losing scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's rule errs on the side of strictness, and scholars are lost.

sentences.zh: 陛下選任宰相，必異於庶官；

translations.literal: Your Majesty in selecting and appointing chief ministers must differ from common officials;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rightly treats the choice of chief ministers differently from lesser appointments;

sentences.zh: 精擇長官，必愈於末品。

translations.literal: Carefully selecting department chiefs must exceed low ranks.
translations.idiomatic: and rightly applies stricter scrutiny to department heads than to low ranks.

sentences.zh: 及至宰相獻規，長吏薦士，陛下即但納橫議，不稽始謀。

translations.literal: Yet when chief ministers present regulations and department chiefs recommend scholars, Your Majesty then only accepts perverse discussion, not examining the original deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when chief ministers offer policy and department heads recommend talent, Your Majesty hears only reckless criticism and does not examine the original proposal.

sentences.zh: 是乃任以重者輕其言，待以輕者重其事，且又不辨所毀之虛實，不校所試之短長。

translations.literal: This is entrusting with heavy matters yet treating their words lightly, treating with light matters yet weighing the affair heavily—and moreover not distinguishing the truth and falsehood of what is slandered, not comparing the strengths and weaknesses of what is tested.
translations.idiomatic: This is to treat grave counsel lightly and petty rumor seriously—not to test what is slandered for truth or falsehood, nor to judge nominees by their actual merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 人之多言，何所不至，是將使人無所措其手足，豈獨選任之道失其端而已乎！

translations.literal: Men's much speaking—what would not they reach! This will cause people nowhere to place their hands and feet—not only that the Way of selection and appointment loses its beginning!
translations.idiomatic: When men talk freely, nothing is spared. People will no longer know where to turn—not in selection alone, but in every affair of state!

sentences.zh: 上雖嘉其所陳，長官薦士之詔，竟追寢之。

translations.literal: The emperor though praising what was laid out, the edict on department chiefs recommending scholars was finally pursued and suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor praised what Lu Zhi had said, the edict allowing department heads to recommend subordinates was in the end withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 國朝舊制，吏部選人，每年調集。

translations.literal: The dynasty's old system: the Ministry of Personnel selected candidates gathered each year.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system of the dynasty, the Ministry of Personnel gathered candidates for appointment every year.

sentences.zh: 自乾元已後，屬宿兵於野。

translations.literal: From after the Qianyuan era, troops were quartered in the field.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianyuan era troops remained encamped in the field.

sentences.zh: 歲或兇荒，遂三年一置選。

translations.literal: Years sometimes had famine and disaster; therefore selections were held once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine the examinations were held only once every three years.

sentences.zh: 由是選人停擁，其數猥多，文書不接，真偽難辨，吏緣為奸，註授乖濫，而有十年不得調者。

translations.literal: From this candidates accumulated in delay, their numbers excessively many—documents not connecting, true and false hard to distinguish, clerks used this for fraud, registration and assignment perverse and excessive, and some went ten years without assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates therefore piled up in great numbers. Records no longer matched, truth and fraud were hard to tell apart, clerks turned the confusion to profit, and appointments became chaotic. Some men waited ten years without receiving a post.

sentences.zh: 贄奏吏部分內外官員為三分，計闕集人，每年置選。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized dividing the Ministry of Personnel's inner and outer officials into three parts, calculating vacant posts and gathered people, holding selection each year.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi proposed dividing the Ministry's inner and outer appointments into three groups, tallying vacancies and candidates, and holding selection every year.

sentences.zh: 故選司之弊，十去七八，天下稱之。

translations.literal: Therefore the Selection Office's abuses were seven or eight tenths gone; all under Heaven praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The abuses of the Selection Office were thereby reduced by seven or eight tenths, and the realm praised the reform.

sentences.zh: 贄與賈耽、盧邁、趙憬同知政事，百司有所申覆，皆更讓不言可否。

translations.literal: Zhi together with Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing jointly managed state affairs; when the hundred offices had submissions and replies, all deferring to one another without saying yes or no.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi served with Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing as joint chief ministers. When offices submitted business for decision, each man deferred to the others and none would say yes or no.

sentences.zh: 舊例，宰臣當旬，秉筆決事，每十日一易，贄請準故事，令秉筆者以應之。

translations.literal: Old precedent: chief ministers in rotation, holding the brush to decide affairs, changing every ten days—Zhi requested following precedent, causing the brush-holder to respond accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: By old precedent the chief ministers took turns holding the brush and deciding affairs, rotating every ten days. Lu Zhi asked that this precedent be restored so that the man holding the brush would answer when called upon.

sentences.zh: 又以河隴陷蕃已來，西北邊常以重兵守備，謂之防秋，皆河南、江淮諸鎮之軍也，更番往來，疲於戍役。

translations.literal: Also because since Hexi and Longyou fell to the Tibetans, the northwest frontier constantly used heavy troops for defense—called autumn defense—all armies of the Henan, Jianghuai, and various commands, rotating back and forth, exhausted by garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hexi and Longyou had fallen to Tibet, the northwest frontier had been held by heavy forces in what was called autumn defense—troops from the Henan, Jianghuai, and other commands rotating in turn, worn out by garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 贄以中原之兵，不習邊事，及扞虜戰賊，多有敗衄，又苦邊將名目太多，諸軍統制不一，緩急無以應敵，乃上疏論其事曰：

translations.literal: Zhi because Central Plains troops did not practice frontier affairs, and in resisting barbarians and fighting bandits many suffered defeat, also suffering from too many frontier generals' titles, the various armies' unified command not one—in urgency and ease having no means to respond to the enemy—then submitted a memorial discussing the matter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi held that the armies of the central plains were unused to frontier warfare and suffered many defeats against barbarians and rebels; that there were too many frontier commanders and no unified command; and that in crisis the forces could not respond effectively. He therefore submitted a memorial on the matter, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣歷觀前代書史，皆謂鎮撫四夷，宰相之任，不揆闇劣，屢敢上言。

translations.literal: Your servant throughout viewing former ages' books and histories—all say pacifying and soothing the four barbarians is the chief minister's charge; not measuring my darkness and inferiority, repeatedly daring to speak above.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has read the histories of former ages and finds that pacifying the four quarters is the chief minister's duty. Ignorant though I am, I have repeatedly ventured to speak.

sentences.zh: 誠以備邊禦戎，國家之重事；

translations.literal: Truly because preparing the frontier and defending against barbarians is the state's weighty affair;
translations.idiomatic: For frontier defense is a weighty affair of state;

sentences.zh: 理兵足食，備禦之大經。

translations.literal: ordering troops and filling granaries is the great constant of defense.
translations.idiomatic: and ordering the armies and filling the granaries is the great foundation of defense.

sentences.zh: 兵不治則無可用之師，食不足則無可固之地。

translations.literal: Troops not ordered then no usable army; food insufficient then no place that can be held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Without well-ordered troops there is no army fit for use; without sufficient grain no land can be held.

sentences.zh: 理兵在制置得所，足食在斂導有方。

translations.literal: Ordering troops lies in disposition being appropriate; filling granaries lies in collection and guidance having method.
translations.idiomatic: Ordering troops depends on proper disposition; filling granaries depends on sound collection and distribution.

sentences.zh: 陛下幸聽愚言，先務積谷，人無加賦，官不費財，坐致邊儲，數逾百萬。

translations.literal: Your Majesty fortunately listening to my foolish words, first task accumulating grain—people without added tax, offices without expending funds, sitting to achieve frontier stores, numbering exceeding a million.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has graciously heeded my counsel and made grain accumulation the first task. Without adding to the people's taxes or wasting public funds, frontier stores now exceed a million.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮收糴，今已向終，分貯軍城，用防艱急，縱有寇戎之患，必無乏絕之憂。

translations.literal: The various commands' grain purchases—now already nearing completion—divided and stored in military cities, used to guard against hardship and urgency; even if there are bandit and barbarian troubles, certainly no fear of exhaustion and cutoff.
translations.idiomatic: The commands' grain purchases are nearly complete, stored in garrison cities against emergency. Even if bandits or barbarians strike, there need be no fear of shortage.

sentences.zh: 守此成規，以為永制，常收冗費，益贍邊農，則更經二年，可積十萬人三歲之糧矣。

translations.literal: Guarding this established rule as perpetual system, constantly gathering surplus expenses, increasing support for frontier farmers—then after two more years, one could accumulate three years' grain for a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: If this rule is kept as a permanent system, surplus funds redirected to support frontier farming, then in two more years there could be three years' grain for a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 足食之原粗立，理兵之術未精，敢議籌量，庶備采擇。

translations.literal: The source of sufficient food roughly established, the art of ordering troops not yet refined—I dare discuss planning and reckoning, hoping to prepare for selection and adoption.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of adequate supply is roughly in place; the art of ordering troops is not yet perfected. I venture to offer further plans for Your Majesty's consideration.

sentences.zh: 伏以戎狄為患，自古有之，其於制禦之方，得失之論，備存史籍，可得而言。

translations.literal: I respectfully submit that the Rong and Di as a menace has existed since antiquity; regarding methods of control and defense, and discussions of success and failure, these are fully preserved in historical records and may be expounded upon.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully, the threat posed by the Rong and Di is as old as history itself. The methods for controlling and defending against them, and the debates over what succeeded and what failed, are all fully recorded in the chronicles—and can be examined at length.

sentences.zh: 大抵尊即序者，則曰「非德無以化要荒」，曾莫知威不立，則德不能馴也。

translations.literal: Generally those who honor bringing into ritual order say, "Without virtue there is no means to transform the remote wilds," yet they never understand that unless authority is established, virtue cannot tame them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who prize the approach of bringing the frontier peoples into ritual order declare that "only virtue can transform the remote borderlands"—yet they never grasp that unless authority is first established, virtue alone cannot make them submit.

sentences.zh: 樂武威者，則曰「非兵無以服兇獷」，曾莫知德不修，則兵不可恃也。

translations.literal: Those who delight in martial prestige say, "Without arms there is no means to subdue the fierce and unruly," yet they never understand that if virtue is not cultivated, arms cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Those who delight in martial power insist that "only force can tame the violent and intractable"—yet they never see that without moral cultivation, military might is not something one can trust.

sentences.zh: 務和親者，則曰「要結可以睦鄰好」，曾莫知我結之而彼復解也。

translations.literal: Those devoted to heqin alliance say, "Binding ties can foster neighborly goodwill," yet they never understand that when we bind them, they again unravel the ties.
translations.idiomatic: Those devoted to alliance through marriage say that "binding ties can preserve neighborly goodwill"—yet they never see that the moment we forge such bonds, our counterparts may break them again.

sentences.zh: 美長城者，則曰「設險可以固邦國而扞寇仇」，曾莫知力不足，兵不堪，則險之不能有也。

translations.literal: Those who praise the Great Wall say, "Establishing defenses can fortify the state and repel enemy invaders," yet they never understand that when strength is insufficient and troops inadequate, defenses cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Those who praise the Great Wall claim that "fortifying strategic passes can secure the realm and ward off enemy raids"—yet they never see that when one's strength is inadequate and one's armies insufficient, no fortification can be held.

sentences.zh: 尚薄伐者，則曰「驅遏可以禁侵暴而省征徭，」曾莫知兵不銳，壘不完，則遏之不能勝，驅之不能去也。

translations.literal: Those who favor limited punitive expeditions say, "Driving back and blocking can forbid aggression and reduce corvée and levies," yet they never understand that when troops are not sharp and fortifications incomplete, blocking cannot prevail and driving cannot remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who favor limited border campaigns argue that "driving the enemy back and blocking incursions can end pillaging and lighten the burden of corvée and levies"—yet they never see that when troops are dull and defenses incomplete, blocking cannot win and driving cannot dislodge the foe.

sentences.zh: 議邊之要，略盡於斯，雖互相譏評，然各有偏駁。

translations.literal: The essentials of discussing border affairs are largely exhausted in these points; though they mutually ridicule and criticize one another, each has its partialities and defects.
translations.idiomatic: The main points debated in discussions of border policy are largely covered by these positions. Though advocates mock one another, each approach is one-sided and flawed in its own way.

sentences.zh: 聽一家之說，則例理可征；

translations.literal: Listening to one school's doctrine, then its principles and reasoning can be verified;
translations.idiomatic: Heed any single school of thought alone, and its logic seems persuasive enough;

sentences.zh: 考歷代所行，則成敗異效。

translations.literal: Examining what was practiced through successive dynasties, then success and failure yield different results.
translations.idiomatic: but examine what successive dynasties actually put into practice, and the outcomes vary from success to failure.

sentences.zh: 是由執常理以禦其不常之勢，徇所見而昧於所遇之時。

translations.literal: This comes from holding to constant principles to defend against inconstant circumstances, and following one's own view while being blind to the times one encounters.
translations.idiomatic: This is what happens when one clings to fixed principles to meet ever-changing circumstances, and pursues one's own preconceptions while failing to read the times.

sentences.zh: 夫中夏有盛衰，夷狄有強弱，事機有利害，措置有安危，故無必定之規，亦無長勝之法。

translations.literal: Now, the Central Realm has its rise and decline, the barbarians have their strength and weakness, opportunities have their benefits and harms, and arrangements have their safety and peril—therefore there is no fixed rule, nor any permanently victorious method.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Realm waxes and wanes; the frontier peoples grow strong and grow weak; circumstances offer both advantage and harm; and any given policy may bring safety or peril. Thus there is no fixed formula, and no strategy that always wins.

sentences.zh: 夏後以序戎而聖化茂，古公以避狄而王業興；

translations.literal: Xia Hou brought the Rong into order and sagely transformation flourished; Lord Ancient avoided the Di and royal enterprise arose;
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia brought the Rong into order, and sage rule flourished; Lord Danfu fled the Di, and a royal dynasty was born;

sentences.zh: 周城朔方而獫狁攘，秦築臨洮而宗社覆；

translations.literal: Zhou fortified Shuofang yet the Xianyun raided; Qin built at Lintao yet the ancestral altars fell;
translations.idiomatic: the Zhou fortified Shuofang, yet the Xianyun raided all the more; Qin built fortifications at Lintao, yet the dynasty itself was destroyed;

sentences.zh: 漢武討匈奴而貽悔，太宗征突厥而致安；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han campaigned against the Xiongnu and bequeathed regret; Emperor Taizong campaigned against the Turks and achieved peace;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han campaigned against the Xiongnu and left posterity with regret; Emperor Taizong campaigned against the Turks and brought peace;

sentences.zh: 文、景約和親而不能弭患於當年，宣、元弘撫納而足以保寧於累葉。

translations.literal: Wen and Jing made heqin treaties yet could not quell the trouble in their own age; Xuan and Yuan broadly embraced and received them and were sufficient to preserve tranquility for successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Jing negotiated marriage alliances but could not end the troubles of their day; Emperors Xuan and Yuan pursued a policy of conciliation and were able to secure peace for generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 蓋以中夏之盛衰異勢，夷狄之強弱異時，事機之利害異情，措置之安危異便。

translations.literal: This is because the Central Realm's rise and decline differ in circumstance, the barbarians' strength and weakness differ in time, opportunities' benefits and harms differ in nature, and arrangements' safety and peril differ in suitability.
translations.idiomatic: For the rise and fall of the Central Realm follows one set of circumstances, the strength and weakness of the frontier peoples another; the benefits and harms of any given situation another still; and the safety or peril of any given policy depends on what the moment requires.

sentences.zh: 知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。

translations.literal: Knowing the matter but not gauging the times leads to failure; adhering to the times without losing what is fitting leads to success.
translations.idiomatic: To understand the problem but misread the times is to fail; to follow the demands of the moment without abandoning what is appropriate is to succeed.

sentences.zh: 形變不同，胡可專一！

translations.literal: Forms and changes are not the same—how can one be devoted to a single approach!
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances change—how can one cling to a single method!

sentences.zh: 夫以中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而能屈膝稱臣，歸心受制，拒之則阻其向化，威之則類於殺降，安得不存而撫之，即而序之也？

translations.literal: Now, when China is strong and flourishing and the barbarians are weak and declining, and they are able to bend the knee as subjects and turn their hearts to submission—if one rejects them one obstructs their turning toward civilization; if one threatens them it is like killing those who surrender—how can one not preserve and soothe them, approach them and bring them into order?
translations.idiomatic: When China is strong and the frontier peoples weak, and they come kneeling as subjects, their hearts turned toward obedience—to reject them would block their turning toward civilization; to threaten them would be little better than slaughtering men who have surrendered. How can the court do anything but protect and conciliate them, draw them close, and bring them into proper order?

sentences.zh: 又如中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而尚棄信奸盟，蔑恩肆毒，諭之不變，責之不懲，安得不取亂推亡，息人固境也？

translations.literal: Again, if China is strong and flourishing and the barbarians are weak and declining, yet they still abandon faith, break alliances treacherously, scorn kindness and unleash cruelty, and instruction does not change them nor censure chastise them—how can one not take their disorder to push them to destruction, give rest to the people and fortify the borders?
translations.idiomatic: Or again: when China is strong and the frontier peoples weak, yet they betray their oaths, break alliances in bad faith, spurn kindness and unleash violence, and neither persuasion nor reproach can move them—how can the court do anything but seize on their disorder to bring about their downfall, spare its own people, and secure the borders?

sentences.zh: 其有遇中國喪亡之弊，當夷狄強盛之時，圖之則彼釁未萌，禦之則我力不足，安得不卑詞降禮，約好通和，啖之以親，紓其交禍？

translations.literal: When one encounters China's decline and ruin, at a time when the barbarians are strong and flourishing—if one plots against them their provocation has not yet emerged; if one defends against them our strength is insufficient—how can one not use humble words and lowered ceremony, covenant for friendship and open harmony, appease them with intimacy, and relieve the mutual calamity of conflict?
translations.idiomatic: When China is in decline and the frontier peoples are ascendant—plot against them and no provocation has yet arisen; try to resist and one's strength is not enough—how can the court do anything but speak humbly, lower its ceremonial demeanor, seek treaties of friendship, appease them with conciliatory overtures, and avert the disaster of open conflict?

sentences.zh: 縱不必信，且無大侵，雖非禦戎之善經，蓋時事亦有不得已也。

translations.literal: Even if one need not fully trust them, and there are no major incursions, though this is not the best constant practice for controlling the Rong, yet in the circumstances of the times there are also things one cannot avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Even if such agreements cannot be fully trusted, and even if no major invasion follows, this may not be the ideal long-term policy for managing the frontier—yet there are times when circumstances leave no alternative.

sentences.zh: 儻或夷夏之勢，強弱適同，撫之不寧，威之不靖；

translations.literal: If perhaps the strength of barbarians and Chinese are equally matched, soothing does not bring peace and threatening does not bring tranquility;
translations.idiomatic: Should the power of the frontier peoples and the Central Realm be evenly matched—so that conciliation cannot secure peace and intimidation cannot restore calm—

sentences.zh: 力足以自保，不足以出攻，得不設險以固軍，訓師以待寇，來則薄伐以遏其深入，去則攘斥而戒於遠追？

translations.literal: Strength sufficient to protect oneself but insufficient to sally forth in attack—must one not establish defenses to fortify the army, train troops to await raiders, when they come conduct limited campaigns to block their deep penetration, and when they depart drive them off yet refrain from distant pursuit?
translations.idiomatic: and one's strength is enough to defend but not enough to take the offensive—must one not fortify strategic positions, drill the army to await attack, meet incursions with limited counter-raids to check deep penetration, and when the enemy withdraws, drive them off without pursuing too far?

sentences.zh: 雖為安邊之令圖，蓋勢力亦有不得不然也。

translations.literal: Though this is the excellent plan for securing the borders, it is also that circumstances of power leave no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: Though this is the soundest plan for securing the borders, the balance of power may also leave no other choice.

sentences.zh: 故夏之即序，周之於攘，太宗之翦亂，皆乘其時而善用其勢也。

translations.literal: Therefore Xia's bringing into order, Zhou's repelling, Taizong's cutting down disorder—all seized their times and well employed their circumstances of power.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yu's bringing the Rong into order, the Zhou's repelling of invaders, and Taizong's suppression of rebellion—all seized the moment and made the best use of prevailing conditions.

sentences.zh: 古公之避狄，文、景之和親，神堯之降禮，皆順其時而不失其稱也。

translations.literal: Lord Ancient's avoiding the Di, Wen and Jing's heqin, Emperor Shenyao's lowered ceremony—all followed the times without losing what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Danfu's flight from the Di, the heqin policies of Emperors Wen and Jing, and Emperor Gaozu's lowered ceremonial demeanor—all conformed to the times without sacrificing what was appropriate.

sentences.zh: 秦皇之長城，漢武之窮討，皆知其事而不度其時者也。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang's Great Wall and Emperor Wu of Han's exhaustive campaigns—both knew the matter but did not gauge the times.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang's Great Wall and Emperor Wu's endless campaigns both understood the problem but failed to read the times.

sentences.zh: 向若遇孔熾之勢，行即序之方，則見侮而不從矣！

translations.literal: If one had encountered overwhelmingly fierce circumstances and pursued the method of bringing into order, then one would be insulted and they would not obey!
translations.idiomatic: Had one pursued a policy of orderly submission in a moment of overwhelming enemy strength, one would only be mocked—and they would refuse to obey!

sentences.zh: 乘可取之資，懷畏避之誌，則失機而養寇矣！

translations.literal: Seizing resources that could be taken, yet harboring a will of fear and avoidance, one loses opportunity and nourishes the raiders!
translations.idiomatic: To hold the advantage for decisive action yet shrink back in fear is to miss one's chance and feed the enemy's strength!

sentences.zh: 有攘卻之力，用和親之謀，則示弱而勞費矣！

translations.literal: Having the power to repel and drive back, yet employing heqin strategy, one shows weakness and wastes resources!
translations.idiomatic: To have the power to drive the enemy back yet resort to marriage alliances is to show weakness and squander resources!

sentences.zh: 當降屈之時，務翦伐之略，則召禍而危殆矣！

translations.literal: When one should submit and yield, yet devoting oneself to aggressive campaigns, one invites calamity and peril!
translations.idiomatic: To pursue aggressive campaigns when one ought to submit is to invite disaster and court destruction!

sentences.zh: 故曰：知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: knowing the matter but not gauging the times leads to failure; adhering to the times without losing what is fitting leads to success.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: to understand the problem but misread the times is to fail; to follow the demands of the moment without abandoning what is appropriate is to succeed.

sentences.zh: 是無必定之規，亦無長勝之法，得失著效，不其然歟！

translations.literal: Thus there is no fixed rule, nor any permanently victorious method—the gains and losses prove themselves. Is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: There is no fixed formula and no strategy that always wins—the gains and losses speak for themselves. Is it not so?

sentences.zh: 至於察安危之大情，計成敗之大數，百代之不變易者，蓋有之矣。

translations.literal: As for discerning the great principle of safety and peril, calculating the great pattern of success and failure—among things unchanged for a hundred generations, these exist.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in discerning the great principle of safety and peril, and calculating the great pattern of success and failure, there are truths that hold across a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 其要在於失人肆欲則必蹶，任人從眾則必全，此乃古今所同，而物理之所壹也。

translations.literal: The crux lies in this: lose the support of people through indulgence of desires and one must stumble; employ people and follow the consensus and one must be preserved. This is the same in ancient and modern times—the single principle of natural order.
translations.idiomatic: The crux is this: to alienate the people through indulgence of one's desires is to invite collapse; to employ the worthy and heed the consensus is to preserve the state. This has been true in every age—it is the one constant principle of nature.

sentences.zh: 國家自祿山構亂、河隴用兵以來，肅宗中興，撤邊備以靖中邦，借外威以寧內難。

translations.literal: Since the state, from An Lushan's rebellion and campaigns in Hexi and Longyou, when Emperor Suzong restored the dynasty, withdrew border defenses to pacify the Central Plain, and borrowed foreign military might to quell internal troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Since An Lushan's rebellion and the campaigns in Hexi and Longyou, the dynasty—when Emperor Suzong restored order—withdrew frontier defenses to pacify the Central Plain and borrowed foreign military power to quell internal strife.

sentences.zh: 於是吐蕃乘釁，吞噬無厭；

translations.literal: Thereupon Tibet seized the opportunity, swallowing territory insatiably;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Tibet seized the opportunity and swallowed territory without end;

sentences.zh: 回紇矜功，憑陵亦甚。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs flaunted their merits and were also extremely overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: the Uyghurs flaunted their contributions and grew ever more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 中國不遑振旅，四十余年。

translations.literal: China had no leisure to restore its armies—for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: For more than forty years China had no leisure to rebuild its armies.

sentences.zh: 使傷耗遺氓，竭力蠶織，西輸賄幣，北償馬資，尚不足塞其煩言，滿其驕誌。

translations.literal: This caused the surviving populace to be depleted, straining themselves at sericulture and weaving, sending tribute westward and paying for horses northward—yet still insufficient to stop their vexatious demands and satisfy their proud ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: The surviving populace was worn down, straining at sericulture and weaving to send tribute westward and pay for horses northward—yet still could not satisfy their endless demands or their proud ambitions.

sentences.zh: 復乃遠征士馬，列戍疆陲，猶不能遏其奔沖，止其侵侮。

translations.literal: Moreover they dispatched troops on distant campaigns and stationed garrisons along the borders, yet still could not check their wild charges or stop their raids.
translations.idiomatic: Even when troops were sent on distant campaigns and garrisons lined the frontiers, their wild charges could not be checked nor their raids stopped.

sentences.zh: 小入則驅略黎庶，深入則震驚邦畿。

translations.literal: Small incursions meant plundering the common people; deep penetration shook the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Small raids plundered the common people; deep incursions shook the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 時有議安邊策者，多務於所難而忽於所易，勉於所短而略於所長。

translations.literal: When border pacification policies were debated, most devoted themselves to what was difficult and neglected what was easy, strained at what was their weakness and overlooked what was their strength.
translations.idiomatic: When border policies were debated, most devoted themselves to what was difficult and neglected what was easy, strained at their weaknesses and overlooked their strengths.

sentences.zh: 遂使所易所長者，行之而其要不精；

translations.literal: Thus what was easy and their strength—when implemented, its essentials were not refined;
translations.idiomatic: Thus what was easy and within their strength was pursued without mastering its essentials;

sentences.zh: 所難所短者，圖之而其功靡就。

translations.literal: What was difficult and their weakness—when plotted, the achievement was never accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: while what was difficult and beyond their strength was attempted without ever achieving success.

sentences.zh: 憂患未弭，職斯之由。

translations.literal: Calamities not yet settled—this is precisely the reason.
translations.idiomatic: That calamities remain unabated is precisely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 夫制敵行師，必量事勢，勢有難易，事有先後。

translations.literal: In controlling enemies and deploying armies, one must measure circumstances of affairs; circumstances have easy and difficult aspects, affairs have prior and posterior order.
translations.idiomatic: In controlling enemies and deploying armies, one must weigh the circumstances; circumstances differ in difficulty, and affairs have their proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 力大而敵脆，則先其所難，是謂奪人之心，暫勞而永逸者也；

translations.literal: When strength is great and the enemy fragile, then strike first at what is difficult—this is called seizing the enemy's heart, temporary toil for permanent ease;
translations.idiomatic: When one's strength is great and the enemy weak, strike first at what is difficult—this is called seizing the enemy's will: temporary hardship for lasting peace;

sentences.zh: 力寡而敵堅，則先其所易，是謂固國之本，觀釁而後動者也。

translations.literal: When strength is slight and the enemy firm, then strike first at what is easy—this is called securing the foundation of the state, observing provocation before acting.
translations.idiomatic: When one's strength is slight and the enemy strong, strike first at what is easy—this is called securing the foundation of the state: watch for provocation before acting.

sentences.zh: 頃屬多故，人勞未瘳，而欲廣發師徒，深踐寇境，復其侵地，攻其堅城，前有勝負未必之虞，後有饋運不繼之患。

translations.literal: Recently, amid many troubles, the people's exhaustion not yet healed, yet wishing to broadly dispatch armies, deeply penetrate enemy territory, recover invaded lands, attack fortified cities—ahead lies uncertainty of victory or defeat, behind lies the peril of supply lines not continuing.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, amid many troubles, with the people's exhaustion not yet healed, some wish to dispatch armies in force, penetrate deep into enemy territory, recover lost lands, and assault fortified cities—facing uncertainty of victory ahead and the peril of broken supply lines behind.

sentences.zh: 儻或撓敗，適所以啟戎心而挫國威，以此為安邊之謀，可謂不量事勢而務於所難矣！

translations.literal: If perchance defeated, this would precisely awaken the barbarians' boldness and damage national prestige—to take this as border pacification strategy is truly not measuring circumstances of affairs and devoting oneself to what is difficult!
translations.idiomatic: If defeated, this would only embolden the barbarians and damage national prestige. To take such a course as a border policy is truly to ignore the circumstances and devote oneself to what is hardest!

sentences.zh: 天之授者，有分事，無全功；

translations.literal: What Heaven bestows: there is division of tasks, no complete achievement in all;
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven bestows comes with divided tasks, not complete mastery of all;

sentences.zh: 地之產者，有物宜，無兼利。

translations.literal: What Earth produces: each thing has its proper suitability, no combined benefit in all.
translations.idiomatic: what Earth produces suits each thing in its own way, not every advantage at once.

sentences.zh: 是以五方之俗，長短各殊。

translations.literal: Thus the customs of the five directions each have their own strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the customs of the five directions each have their own strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 長者不可逾，短者不可企；

translations.literal: What is long cannot be exceeded; what is short cannot be reached for;
translations.idiomatic: Strengths cannot be surpassed by force of will; weaknesses cannot be wished away;

sentences.zh: 勉所短而敵其所長必殆，用所長而乘其所短必安。

translations.literal: Straining at what is short and matching against what is long leads to peril; using what is long and exploiting what is short leads to safety.
translations.idiomatic: to strain at one's weaknesses and contest the enemy's strengths is to court disaster; to employ one's strengths and exploit the enemy's weaknesses is to secure safety.

sentences.zh: 強者，乃以水草為邑居，以射獵供飲茹，多馬而尤便馳突，輕生而不恥敗亡，此戎狄之所長也。

translations.literal: The strong ones dwell by water and grass as their settlements, sustain themselves by hunting for food and drink, have many horses and are especially adept at swift cavalry charges, hold life lightly and do not shame defeat and death—this is what the Rong and Di excel at.
translations.idiomatic: The strong dwell by water and grass, live by hunting, keep many horses and excel at swift cavalry charges, hold life lightly and do not fear defeat or death—this is what the Rong and Di do best.

sentences.zh: 戎狄之所長，乃中國之所短；

translations.literal: What the Rong and Di excel at is precisely what China is deficient in;
translations.idiomatic: What the Rong and Di do best is precisely what China does worst;

sentences.zh: 而欲益兵蒐乘，角力爭驅，交鋒原野之間，決命尋常之內，以此為禦寇之術，可謂勉所短而校其所長矣！

translations.literal: Yet wishing to increase troops and gather chariots, contending in strength and racing in driving, clashing on open plains and deciding life and death within ordinary range—to take this as the method of repelling raiders is truly straining at what is short and comparing against what is long!
translations.idiomatic: yet to mass troops and chariots, contest strength in open pursuit, and decide life and death on the plain—to take this as the method of repelling raiders is truly to strain at one's weaknesses and measure oneself against the enemy's strengths!

sentences.zh: 務所難，勉所短，勞費百倍，終於無成。

translations.literal: Devoting oneself to what is difficult, straining at what is short—labor and expense a hundredfold, ending in no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: To devote oneself to what is difficult and strain at what is weak costs a hundredfold in labor and expense, and ends in failure.

sentences.zh: 雖果成之，不挫則廢，豈不以越天授而違地產，虧時勢以反物宜者哉！

translations.literal: Even if one truly succeeded, without setback it would be abandoned—is this not because one transgresses Heaven's bestowal and violates Earth's products, damages circumstances of the times and reverses each thing's proper suitability!
translations.idiomatic: Even if one succeeded, the effort could not be sustained without ruin—is this not because one transgresses Heaven's allotment, violates Earth's natural suitability, and works against the demands of the times!

sentences.zh: 將欲去危就安，息費從省，在慎守所易，精用所長而已。

translations.literal: If one wishes to leave peril and attain safety, cease waste and follow economy, it lies in carefully guarding what is easy and skillfully employing what is long—nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: To leave peril for safety, and end waste through economy, one need only carefully hold to what is easy and skillfully employ what one does best.

sentences.zh: 若乃擇將吏以撫寧眾庶，修紀律以訓齊師徒，耀德以佐威，能邇以柔遠；

translations.literal: As for selecting generals and officials to pacify and settle the populace, refining discipline to train and align troops, displaying virtue to assist authority, being able with what is near to soften what is far;
translations.idiomatic: Select capable generals and officials to pacify the people; refine discipline to train the troops; let displayed virtue support authority, and let competence at home soften those abroad;

sentences.zh: 禁侵抄之暴以彰吾信，抑攻取之議以安戎心；

translations.literal: Forbidding the violence of raids and pillaging to manifest our trustworthiness, suppressing proposals for offensive seizure to settle the barbarians' hearts;
translations.idiomatic: forbid the violence of border raids to demonstrate good faith, and suppress proposals for offensive seizure to reassure the barbarians;

sentences.zh: 彼求和則善待而勿與結盟，彼為寇則嚴備而不務報復，此當今之所易也。

translations.literal: When they seek peace, treat them well but do not enter alliances with them; when they raid, prepare strictly but do not pursue retaliation—this is what is easy in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: When they seek peace, treat them well but do not bind them in formal alliance; when they raid, prepare strictly but do not pursue revenge—this is what is easy in the present age.

sentences.zh: 賤力而貴智，惡殺而好生，輕利而重人，忍小以全大，安其居而後動，俟其時而後行。

translations.literal: Valuing wisdom over brute force, hating killing and loving life, holding profit lightly and people heavily, enduring small losses to preserve the great, settling one's position before acting, awaiting the right moment before moving.
translations.idiomatic: Value wisdom over brute force; hate killing and cherish life; hold profit lightly and people dearly; endure small losses to preserve the greater good; settle one's position before acting, and wait for the right moment before moving.

sentences.zh: 是以修封疆，守要害，塹蹊隧，壘軍營，謹禁防，明斥候，務農以足食，練卒以蓄威，非萬全不謀，非百克不鬥。

translations.literal: Thus repair borders, hold strategic passes, trench paths and tunnels, fortify camps, strictly guard defenses, clearly post scouts, devote to agriculture to fill granaries, drill soldiers to store up might—do not plan without perfect readiness, do not fight without assurance of hundredfold victory.
translations.idiomatic: Thus repair the borders, hold strategic passes, trench roads and tunnels, fortify camps, guard defenses strictly, post scouts clearly, devote to farming to fill the granaries, and drill soldiers to store up strength—do not plan without perfect readiness, and do not fight without assurance of overwhelming victory.

sentences.zh: 寇小至則張聲勢以遏其入，寇大至則謀其人以邀其歸；

translations.literal: When raiders come in small numbers, display force to block their entry; when raiders come in large numbers, plot against their leaders to intercept their return;
translations.idiomatic: When raiders come in small numbers, display force to block their entry; when they come in force, plot against their leaders to cut off their retreat;

sentences.zh: 據險以乘之，多方以誤之。

translations.literal: Hold the terrain and exploit it against them, use many stratagems to mislead them.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the terrain and turn it against them; use many stratagems to confuse them.

sentences.zh: 使其勇無所加，眾無所用；

translations.literal: Cause their courage to have nothing to apply, their numbers to have no use;
translations.idiomatic: Render their courage useless and their numbers impotent;

sentences.zh: 掠則靡獲，攻則不能；

translations.literal: When they plunder they gain nothing, when they attack they cannot succeed;
translations.idiomatic: when they plunder they gain nothing; when they attack they cannot prevail;

sentences.zh: 進有腹背受敵之虞，退有首尾難救之患，所謂乘其弊，不戰而屈人之兵，此中國之所長也。

translations.literal: Advancing they face the peril of enemies front and rear; retreating they face the trouble of head and tail hard to rescue—what is called exploiting their weakness, subduing the enemy's army without battle—this is what China excels at.
translations.idiomatic: advancing they face enemies before and behind; retreating they find no rescue possible—what is called exploiting their weakness and subduing the enemy without battle. This is what China does best.

sentences.zh: 我之所長，乃戎狄之所短；

translations.literal: What we excel at is precisely what the Rong and Di are deficient in;
translations.idiomatic: What we do best is precisely what the Rong and Di do worst;

sentences.zh: 我之所易，乃戎狄之所難。

translations.literal: What is easy for us is precisely what is difficult for the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: what is easy for us is precisely what is hard for them.

sentences.zh: 以長制短，則用力寡而見功多；

translations.literal: Using the long to control the short, then effort applied is slight yet achievements seen are many;
translations.idiomatic: Use strength against weakness, and little effort yields great results;

sentences.zh: 以易敵難，則財不匱而事速就。

translations.literal: Using the easy to match the difficult, then wealth is not exhausted and affairs are quickly accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: use the easy against the hard, and resources are not exhausted while success comes quickly.

sentences.zh: 舍此不務，而反為所乘，斯謂倒持戈矛，以钅尊授寇者也！

translations.literal: Abandoning this and not devoting oneself to it, yet instead being exploited by them—this is what is called holding one's spear and halberd reversed, handing the socket to the raider!
translations.idiomatic: To abandon this and instead be exploited by the enemy is what is called holding one's weapons reversed and handing the hilt to the raider!

sentences.zh: 今則皆務之矣，猶且守封未固，寇戎未懲者，其病在於謀無定用，眾無適從。

translations.literal: Now all devote themselves to it, yet still border defenses are not secure and raiders are not chastised—the flaw lies in plans having no fixed application and the multitude having no clear direction to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though all now profess to pursue this course, the borders remain unsecured and the raiders undeterred—the flaw lies in plans without fixed application and the multitude without clear direction.

sentences.zh: 所任不必才，才者不必任；

translations.literal: Those appointed are not necessarily capable; the capable are not necessarily appointed;
translations.idiomatic: Those appointed are not necessarily capable; the capable are not necessarily appointed;

sentences.zh: 所聞不必實，實者不必聞；

translations.literal: What is heard is not necessarily true; what is true is not necessarily heard;
translations.idiomatic: what is heard is not necessarily true; what is true is not necessarily heard;

sentences.zh: 所信不必誠，誠者不必信；

translations.literal: What is trusted is not necessarily sincere; the sincere are not necessarily trusted;
translations.idiomatic: what is trusted is not necessarily sincere; the sincere are not necessarily trusted;

sentences.zh: 所行不必當，當者未必行。

translations.literal: What is done is not necessarily fitting; what is fitting is not necessarily done.
translations.idiomatic: what is done is not necessarily right; what is right is not necessarily done.

sentences.zh: 故令措置乖方，課責虧度；

translations.literal: Thus orders are arranged wrongly, assessment and responsibility fall short of measure;
translations.idiomatic: Thus policy is misdirected and accountability falls short;

sentences.zh: 財匱於兵眾，力分於將多，怨生於不均，機失於遙制。

translations.literal: Wealth is exhausted by numerous troops, strength divided among many generals, resentment born from inequality, opportunity lost through remote control.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury depleted by excessive troops, strength divided among too many generals, resentment born of inequity, opportunity lost through remote control.

sentences.zh: 臣請為陛下粗陳六者之失，惟明主慎聽而熟察之：

translations.literal: Your servant requests to briefly set forth for Your Majesty the faults of these six points—may the enlightened ruler listen carefully and examine them closely:
translations.idiomatic: Your servant requests to outline for Your Majesty the faults in these six areas—may the enlightened ruler listen carefully and examine them closely:

sentences.zh: 臣聞工欲善其事，必先利其器；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: if a craftsman wishes to do his work well, he must first sharpen his tools;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that if a craftsman wishes to do his work well, he must first sharpen his tools;

sentences.zh: 武欲勝其敵，必先練其兵。

translations.literal: If a warrior wishes to defeat his enemy, he must first drill his troops.
translations.idiomatic: if a warrior wishes to defeat his enemy, he must first drill his troops.

sentences.zh: 練兵之中，所用復異。

translations.literal: Among methods of drilling troops, what is employed also differs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among methods of drilling troops, what is employed also differs.

sentences.zh: 用之於救急，則權以紓難；

translations.literal: Employed for emergency relief, then use expedient measures to ease crisis;
translations.idiomatic: Employed for emergency relief, troops are used flexibly to ease crisis;

sentences.zh: 用之於暫敵，則緩以應機。

translations.literal: Employed for temporary enemy engagement, then use flexibility to respond to opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: employed for temporary engagement with the enemy, they are deployed flexibly to seize opportunity.

sentences.zh: 故事有便宜，而不拘常制；

translations.literal: Thus affairs have what is expedient, without being bound by regular regulations;
translations.idiomatic: Thus affairs have their expedients, unconstrained by regular regulations;

sentences.zh: 謀有奇詭，而不徇眾情。

translations.literal: Plans have strange stratagems, without following popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: and plans have their stratagems, unconstrained by popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 進退死生，唯將所命，此所謂攻討之兵也！

translations.literal: Advance, retreat, life and death—all at the general's command—this is what is called offensive campaigning troops!
translations.idiomatic: Advance, retreat, life and death—all at the general's command. These are what are called offensive campaigning troops!

sentences.zh: 用之於屯戍，則事資可久；

translations.literal: Employed for garrison duty, then affairs rely on what can endure;
translations.idiomatic: Employed for garrison duty, affairs depend on what can endure;

sentences.zh: 勢異從權，非物理所愜不寧，非人情所欲不固。

translations.literal: Circumstances differ so follow expedient authority—unless nature's principles are satisfied there is no peace, unless human sentiment desires it there is no stability.
translations.idiomatic: circumstances differ, so one follows expedient measures—unless natural conditions are satisfied there is no peace, unless human sentiment is accommodated there is no stability.

sentences.zh: 夫人情者，利焉則勸，習焉則安，保親戚則樂生，顧家業則忘死，故可以理術馭，不可以法制驅，此所謂鎮守之兵也。

translations.literal: Now human sentiment: where there is profit one is encouraged, where there is habit one is at ease, protecting kin one loves life, looking to family estate one forgets death—thus they can be governed by reason and art, but cannot be driven by law and regulation—this is what is called garrison defensive troops.
translations.idiomatic: Human sentiment responds to profit with effort, to habit with ease; men who protect their kin love life, and men who look to their families forget death. Such troops can be governed by reason but cannot be driven by regulation alone. These are what are called garrison defensive troops.

sentences.zh: 夫欲備封疆，禦戎狄，非一朝一夕之事，固當選鎮守之兵以置焉。

translations.literal: Now, to prepare border defenses and control the Rong and Di is not a matter of one morning or one evening—it is right to select garrison troops and station them there.
translations.idiomatic: To prepare the borders and defend against the Rong and Di is not work of a single day—it is right to select garrison troops and station them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 古之善選置者，必量其性習，辨其土宜，察其伎能，知其欲惡。

translations.literal: Those skilled in selection and stationing in antiquity necessarily gauged their natures and habits, distinguished regional suitability, observed their skills and abilities, and knew their desires and aversions.
translations.idiomatic: Those skilled in selection and stationing in antiquity gauged men's natures and habits, distinguished regional suitability, observed their skills, and knew their desires and aversions.

sentences.zh: 用其力而不違其性，齊其俗而不易其宜；

translations.literal: Employing their strength without violating their nature, aligning their customs without changing their suitability;
translations.idiomatic: They employed men's strength without violating their nature, and aligned their customs without forcing them against their proper place.

sentences.zh: 引其善而不責其所不能，禁其非而不處其所不欲。

translations.literal: Leading them by their strengths without holding them responsible for what they cannot do, restraining their faults without placing them in what they do not wish.
translations.idiomatic: They drew out men's strengths without demanding what they could not give, and checked their faults without posting them where they did not wish to be.

sentences.zh: 而又類其紀伍，安其室家，然後能使之樂其居，定其誌，奮其氣勢，結其恩情。

translations.literal: Moreover aligning their ranks and units, settling their households and families—only then could they make them content in their residence, fix their resolve, rouse their martial spirit, and bind their bonds of affection.
translations.idiomatic: They organized their ranks, settled their families—and only then could men be made content where they lived, steady in purpose, bold in spirit, and bound to one another in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 撫之以惠，則感而不驕；

translations.literal: Consoling them with kindness, then they are grateful and not arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: Treat them with kindness and they respond with gratitude, not arrogance;

sentences.zh: 臨之以威，則肅而不怨。

translations.literal: Confronting them with authority, then they are reverent and not resentful.
translations.idiomatic: confront them with authority and they stand in awe without resentment.

sentences.zh: 靡督課而人自為用，弛禁防而眾自不攜。

translations.literal: Without supervision and assessment yet people of themselves apply their efforts; relaxed prohibitions and guards yet the masses of themselves do not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Without heavy supervision men applied themselves; with lighter restrictions the troops did not turn disloyal.

sentences.zh: 故出則足兵，居則足食，守則固，戰則強。

translations.literal: Thus when deployed there were sufficient troops, when stationed sufficient provisions, in defense they were solid, in battle they were strong.
translations.idiomatic: Deployed abroad they were sufficient in numbers; at rest they had enough food; in defense they stood firm; in battle they fought strong.

sentences.zh: 其術無他，便於人情而已矣！

translations.literal: The method had nothing else—it was merely accommodating human sentiment, that is all!
translations.idiomatic: The method was nothing more than this: accommodate human nature!

sentences.zh: 今者散征士卒，分戍邊陲，更代往來，以為守備。

translations.literal: Now scattered conscription of soldiers, divided garrison at the border marches, rotation back and forth, taking this as border defense.
translations.idiomatic: Today soldiers are conscripted from scattered sources, posted in rotation to the frontier marches, and sent back and forth in turn—all this passes for border defense.

sentences.zh: 是則不量性習，不辨土宜，邀其所不能，強其所不欲。

translations.literal: This then does not gauge nature and habit, does not distinguish regional suitability, demands what they cannot do, forces what they do not wish.
translations.idiomatic: This is to ignore men's natures and habits, disregard regional suitability, demand what they cannot give, and force what they do not wish.

sentences.zh: 求廣其數而不考其用，將致其力而不察其情，斯可以為羽衛之儀，而無益於備禦之實也。

translations.literal: Seeking to broaden their numbers without examining their use, about to exert their strength without investigating their sentiments—this can serve as the form of guard escort, but is of no benefit to the substance of border defense.
translations.idiomatic: The state seeks to swell head counts without examining utility, and expects men's exertions without understanding their hearts. Such an army may look the part of a royal guard, but it does nothing for real border defense.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 窮邊之地，千里蕭條，寒風裂膚，驚沙慘目；

translations.literal: The remote frontier—desolate for a thousand li, cold wind splitting skin, startling sand blinding the eyes;
translations.idiomatic: The remote frontier is desolate for a thousand li; cold wind splits the skin and blinding sand stings the eyes;

sentences.zh: 與豺狼為鄰伍，以戰鬥為嬉遊；

translations.literal: Neighboring wolves and jackals, taking battle as sport and play;
translations.idiomatic: men live among wolves and jackals and treat battle as sport;

sentences.zh: 晝則荷戈而耕，夜則倚烽而覘；

translations.literal: By day carrying halberds while plowing, by night leaning on beacon towers to watch;
translations.idiomatic: by day they plow with weapons on their backs, by night they lean on beacon towers to keep watch;

sentences.zh: 日有剽害之慮，永無休暇之娛，地惡人勤，於斯為甚！

translations.literal: Daily fear of plunder and harm, never a moment's leisure for pleasure—the land is harsh and the labor severe, nowhere more so than here!
translations.idiomatic: each day brings fear of raid and slaughter, never a moment's rest for pleasure—the land is harsh and the labor crushing, nowhere more so than here!

sentences.zh: 自非生於其域，習於其風，幼而睹焉，長而安焉，不見樂土而遷焉，則罕能寧其居而狎其敵也。

translations.literal: Unless born in that region, accustomed to its winds, seeing it from youth and settling into it from age, never having known a pleasant land to move to—rarely can one settle contentedly in residence and grow familiar with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Unless a man is born there, raised in its ways, accustomed from childhood and settled in adulthood, never having known a gentler land to move to—rarely can he live content on the frontier or grow familiar with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 關東之地，百物阜殷，從軍之徒，尤被優養。

translations.literal: The lands east of the pass abound in all goods; those who join the army are especially well cared for.
translations.idiomatic: East of the pass the land is rich in every commodity, and those who join the army are especially well cared for.

sentences.zh: 慣於溫飽，狎於歡康，比諸邊隅，若異天地。

translations.literal: Accustomed to warmth and full bellies, familiar with ease and comfort—compared to the border corners, it is as if another heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Accustomed to warmth and full bellies, to ease and comfort—they might as well live in another world from the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 聞絕塞荒陬之苦，則辛酸動容；

translations.literal: Hearing of the bitter hardships of the far frontier wastes, their faces twist with anguish;
translations.idiomatic: Hear of the bitter hardships of the far frontier and their faces twist with anguish;

sentences.zh: 聆強蕃勁虜之名，則懾駭奪氣。

translations.literal: Hearing the names of powerful fan tribes and fierce enemies, they are seized with terror and lose their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: hear the names of powerful barbarian tribes and fierce enemies and terror steals their breath.

sentences.zh: 而乃使之去親族，舍園廬，甘其所辛酸，抗其所懾駭，將冀為用，不亦疏乎！

translations.literal: Yet you would have them leave their kin, abandon their homes and gardens, accept those bitter hardships, and stand against what fills them with terror—and still expect them to be useful? How far-fetched!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would have them leave their kin, abandon their homes, accept those bitter hardships, and stand against what fills them with terror—and still expect them to be useful? How far-fetched!

sentences.zh: 矧又有休代之期，無統帥之馭，資奉若驕子，姑息如倩人，進不邀之以成功，退不處之以嚴憲。

translations.literal: Moreover there are periods of relief and rotation, no commanding general's control; provisions and pay as for spoiled children, indulgence as for hired hands; on advance not urged toward success, on retreat not held to strict discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they serve on fixed rotations under no commanding general's firm hand; rations and pay are lavished on them like spoiled children, indulgence extended like hired laborers; on advance they are not pressed toward victory, on retreat they are not held to strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 其來也鹹負得色，其止也莫有固心，屈指計歸，張頤待飼。

translations.literal: When they arrive all wear the look of one who has gained something; when they halt none has a steadfast heart; they count on their fingers the days till return, mouths open awaiting rations.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrive, all wear the look of men who have gained something; once posted, none has a steadfast heart. They count on their fingers the days till rotation, mouths open awaiting rations.

sentences.zh: 僥倖者猶患還期之賒緩，常念戎醜之充斥；

translations.literal: Even the fortunate still worry that the rotation period will be delayed, constantly mindful that enemy raiders fill the land;
translations.idiomatic: Even the fortunate still worry that rotation will be delayed, constantly mindful that enemy raiders fill the land;

sentences.zh: 王師挫傷，則將乘其亂離，布路東潰，情誌且爾，得之奚為？

translations.literal: If the imperial armies suffer defeat, they will seize the disorder to scatter eastward along every road—their hearts and wills being thus, what use is there in having them?
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial armies suffer defeat, they will seize the disorder to scatter eastward along every road—their hearts and wills being thus, what use is there in having them?

sentences.zh: 平居則殫耗資儲以奉浮冗之眾，臨難則拔棄城鎮以搖遠近之心，其弊豈惟無益哉！
