translations.literal: In ordinary times they exhaust stores and resources to support this idle redundant host; in crisis they abandon towns and forts and shake the hearts of near and far—the harm is not merely that they are useless!
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times they drain stores and resources to support this idle, redundant host; in crisis they abandon towns and forts and shake the hearts of near and far—the harm is not merely that they are useless!

sentences.zh: 固亦將有所撓也。

translations.literal: They will also undermine our position.
translations.idiomatic: They will also undermine our position.

sentences.zh: 復有抵犯刑禁，謫徙軍城，意欲增戶實邊，兼令展效自贖。

translations.literal: There are also those who violate criminal prohibitions, exiled to garrison towns—the intent being to increase households and populate the border, and also to let them redeem themselves through service.
translations.idiomatic: There are also criminals exiled to garrison towns—the intent being to increase households and populate the border, and also to let them redeem themselves through service.

sentences.zh: 既是無良之類，且加懷土之情，思亂幸災，又甚戍卒。

translations.literal: Since they are already worthless types, and with the added attachment to home soil, longing for disorder and hoping for disaster—they are worse than regular garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They are already worthless men, and with their attachment to home they long for disorder and hope for disaster—they are worse than ordinary garrison soldiers.

sentences.zh: 適足煩於防衛，諒無望於功庸，雖前代時或行之，固非良算之可遵者也。

translations.literal: They merely add to the burden of defense, surely with no hope of achievement; though former dynasties sometimes employed this policy, it is certainly not a sound plan to follow.
translations.idiomatic: They merely add to the burden of defense, with no hope of achievement; though former dynasties sometimes employed this policy, it is certainly not a sound plan to follow.

sentences.zh: 復有擁旄之帥，身不臨邊，但分偏師，俾守疆場。

translations.literal: There are also commanders bearing banners and staffs who do not personally go to the border, but only assign detached units to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: There are also commanders bearing banners and staffs who never go to the border themselves, but only assign detached units to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 大抵軍中壯銳，元戎例選自隨，委其疲羸，乃配諸鎮。

translations.literal: Generally the strong and sharp troops in the army—the supreme commander as a rule selects for his own following, consigning the worn and weak to be assigned to the garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule the supreme commander keeps the army's strongest and sharpest troops for himself and consigns the worn and weak to the garrisons.

sentences.zh: 節將既居內地，精兵祗備紀綱，遂令守要禦沖，常在寡弱之輩。

translations.literal: Since the frontier commissioners remain in the interior, elite troops are kept only for discipline and order—and so those who hold key passes and guard approaches are constantly the weak and few.
translations.idiomatic: Since frontier commissioners remain in the interior and elite troops are kept only for discipline and order, those who hold key passes and guard approaches are constantly the weak and few.

sentences.zh: 寇戎每至，乃勢不支，入壘者才足閉關，在野者悉遭劫執，恣其芟蹂，盡其搜驅。

translations.literal: Each time raiders arrive, the garrisons cannot hold; those who enter the ramparts barely manage to shut the gates; those in the open country are all seized in raids; the enemy ravages at will and drives off everything in search.
translations.idiomatic: Each time raiders arrive the garrisons cannot hold; those who reach the ramparts barely manage to shut the gates; those in the open country are all seized. The enemy ravages at will and drives off everything they can find.

sentences.zh: 比及都府聞知，虜已克獲旋返。

translations.literal: By the time the regional headquarters learn of it, the enemy has already taken their plunder and returned.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the regional headquarters learn of it, the enemy has already taken their plunder and returned.

sentences.zh: 且安邊之本，所切在兵，理兵若斯，可謂措置乖方矣！

translations.literal: The foundation of securing the border lies above all in the army—to manage troops in this fashion may be called misplaced arrangements!
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of securing the border lies above all in the army—to manage troops in this fashion is what I call misplaced arrangements!

sentences.zh: 夫賞以存勸，罰以示懲，勸以懋有庸，懲以威不恪。

translations.literal: Rewards exist to preserve encouragement; punishments to show chastisement; encouragement to promote achievement; chastisement to awe the undisciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards exist to preserve encouragement; punishments to show chastisement; encouragement to promote achievement; chastisement to awe the undisciplined.

sentences.zh: 故賞罰之於馭眾也，猶繩墨之於曲直，權衡之揣重輕，輗軏之所以行車，銜勒之所以服馬也。

translations.literal: Thus rewards and punishments in governing the masses are like the carpenter's line for straight and crooked, the balance for weighing heavy and light, the yoke-bar for making the cart go, the bit and reins for making the horse obey.
translations.idiomatic: Thus rewards and punishments in governing troops are like the carpenter's line for straight and crooked, the balance for weighing heavy and light, the yoke-bar that makes the cart go, the bit and reins that make the horse obey.

sentences.zh: 馭眾而不用賞罰，則善惡相混而能否莫殊；

translations.literal: Governing the masses without using rewards and punishments, then good and evil mix together and the capable and incapable are not distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Governing troops without rewards and punishments mixes good and evil until the capable and incapable cannot be told apart;

sentences.zh: 用之而不當功過，則奸妄寵榮而忠實擯抑。

translations.literal: Using them but not matching them to merit and fault, then the treacherous and arrogant are favored with glory while the loyal and honest are pushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: using them but not matching them to merit and fault favors the treacherous and arrogant while pushing aside the loyal and honest.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，若聰明可衒，律度無章，則用與不用，其弊一也。

translations.literal: If matters stand thus—even if one has brilliance to display, if laws and standards are without rule, then using or not using rewards and punishments—the harm is the same.
translations.idiomatic: If matters stand thus—even if one has brilliance to display, if laws and standards are without rule, then using or not using rewards and punishments, the harm is the same.

sentences.zh: 自頃權移於下，柄失於朝，將之號令，既鮮克行之於軍，國之典章，又不能施之於將，務相遵養，茍度歲時。

translations.literal: Recently authority has shifted downward and control been lost at court; commanders' orders rarely prevail in the army, and the state's statutes cannot be enforced upon generals—they merely watch over one another indulgently, passing the years as they may.
translations.idiomatic: Recently authority has shifted downward and control been lost at court; commanders' orders rarely prevail in the army, and the state's statutes cannot be enforced upon generals—they merely watch over one another indulgently, passing the years as they may.

sentences.zh: 欲賞一有功，翻慮無功者反側；

translations.literal: Wishing to reward one who has merit, one instead worries that the meritless will grow restless;
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to reward one who has merit, one instead worries that the meritless will grow restless;

sentences.zh: 欲罰一有罪，復慮同惡者憂虞。

translations.literal: Wishing to punish one who is guilty, one again worries that fellow evildoers will be anxious.
translations.idiomatic: wishing to punish one who is guilty, one again worries that fellow evildoers will be anxious.

sentences.zh: 罪以隱忍而不彰，功以嫌疑而不賞，姑息之道，乃至於斯。

translations.literal: Crimes are hidden and tolerated rather than exposed; merit is left unrewarded through suspicion—the way of indulgence has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes are hidden and tolerated rather than exposed; merit is left unrewarded through suspicion—the way of indulgence has reached this point.

sentences.zh: 故使忘身效節者，獲誚於等夷；

translations.literal: Thus those who forget themselves to serve loyalty are mocked by their peers;
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who forget themselves in loyal service are mocked by their peers;

sentences.zh: 率眾先登者，取怨於士卒；

translations.literal: Those who lead the ranks in the first assault earn the soldiers' resentment;
translations.idiomatic: those who lead the ranks in the first assault earn the soldiers' resentment;

sentences.zh: 僨軍蹙國者，不懷於愧畏；

translations.literal: Those who fail the army and distress the state feel no shame or fear;
translations.idiomatic: those who fail the army and distress the state feel no shame or fear;

sentences.zh: 緩救失期者，自以為智能。

translations.literal: Those who delay relief and miss their deadlines consider themselves clever.
translations.idiomatic: those who delay relief and miss their deadlines consider themselves clever.

sentences.zh: 褒貶既闕而不行，稱毀復紛然相亂，人雖欲善，誰為言之？

translations.literal: Praise and blame being absent and not enforced, slander and praise again swirl in confusion—though men wish to do good, who will speak for them?
translations.idiomatic: With praise and blame absent and unenforced, slander and praise swirl in confusion—though men wish to do good, who will speak for them?

sentences.zh: 況又公忠者，直己而不求於人，反罹困厄；

translations.literal: Moreover the fair and loyal, upright in themselves and not seeking from others, instead suffer hardship;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the fair and loyal, upright in themselves and not seeking from others, instead suffer hardship;

sentences.zh: 敗撓者，行私而茍媚於眾，例獲優崇。

translations.literal: Failures and shirkers, pursuing private ends and fawning on the masses, routinely receive preferment and honor.
translations.idiomatic: failures and shirkers, pursuing private ends and fawning on the masses, routinely receive preferment and honor.

sentences.zh: 此義士所以痛心，勇夫所以解體也。

translations.literal: This is why men of principle are heartbroken and brave men lose their fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: This is why men of principle are heartbroken and brave men lose their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 又有遇敵而所守不固，陳謀而其效靡成；

translations.literal: There are also cases of encountering the enemy but failing to hold what was defended, of laying plans yet achieving no result;
translations.idiomatic: There are also cases of encountering the enemy but failing to hold what was defended, of laying plans yet achieving no result;

sentences.zh: 將帥則以資糧不足為詞，有司復以供給無闕為解。

translations.literal: The generals cite insufficient supplies as their excuse, while the responsible offices reply that provisions were delivered without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: The generals cite insufficient supplies as their excuse, while the responsible offices reply that provisions were delivered without shortage.

sentences.zh: 既相執證，理合辨明，朝廷每為含糊，未嘗窮究曲直。

translations.literal: Since each side holds to its proof, the truth ought to be sorted out—yet the court habitually responds with evasion and never thoroughly investigates right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Since each side holds to its proof, the truth ought to be sorted out—yet the court habitually responds with evasion and never thoroughly investigates right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 措理者吞聲而靡訴，誣善者罔上而不慚。

translations.literal: Those who have managed affairs swallow their words and cannot appeal; those who slander the good deceive their superiors without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Those who have managed affairs swallow their words and cannot appeal; those who slander the good deceive their superiors without shame.

sentences.zh: 馭眾若斯，可謂課責虧度矣！

translations.literal: To govern the masses in this fashion may be called deficient accountability!
translations.idiomatic: To govern troops in this fashion is what I call deficient accountability!

sentences.zh: 課責虧度，措置乖方，將不得竭其材，卒不得盡其力，屯集雖眾，戰陣莫前。

translations.literal: With deficient accountability and misplaced arrangements, generals cannot exhaust their talents, soldiers cannot give their full strength—though gathered in great numbers, none advance in battle.
translations.idiomatic: With deficient accountability and misplaced arrangements, generals cannot exhaust their talents and soldiers cannot give their full strength—though gathered in great numbers, none advance in battle.

sentences.zh: 虜每越境橫行，若涉無人之地；

translations.literal: The enemy crosses the border and rampages at will, as if walking through unoccupied land;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy crosses the border and rampages at will, as if walking through unoccupied land;

sentences.zh: 遞相推倚，無敢誰何，虛張賊勢上聞，則曰兵少不敵。

translations.literal: Each shifts blame to the next, none dares act—and when they falsely inflate the enemy's strength in reports to the throne, they say their troops are too few to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Each shifts blame to the next, none dares act—and when they falsely inflate the enemy's strength in reports to the throne, they say their troops are too few to resist.

sentences.zh: 朝廷莫之省察，惟務征發益師，無裨備禦之功，重增供億之弊。

translations.literal: The court does not examine this, but only presses conscription and reinforcements—adding nothing to border defense, only multiplying the burden of supply.
translations.idiomatic: The court does not examine this, but only presses conscription and reinforcements—adding nothing to border defense, only multiplying the burden of supply.

sentences.zh: 閭井日耗，征求日繁，以編戶傾家破產之資，兼有司榷鹽稅酒之利，總其所入，半以事邊，制用若斯，可謂財匱於兵眾矣！

translations.literal: Registered households dwindle day by day, levies grow daily more oppressive—drawing on resources that ruin families and drain estates, together with monopoly profits on salt, wine, and taxes—of total revenue, half goes to the border. To manage resources thus may be called resources exhausted by the multitude of troops!
translations.idiomatic: Registered households dwindle day by day and levies grow ever more oppressive—drawing on resources that ruin families and drain estates, together with monopoly profits on salt, wine, and taxes. Of total revenue, half goes to the border. To manage resources thus is what I call resources exhausted by the multitude of troops!

sentences.zh: 今四夷之最強盛為中國甚患者，莫大於吐蕃，舉國勝兵之徒，才當中國十數大郡而已。

translations.literal: Among the four barbarians, the strongest and greatest threat to China is none greater than Tibet—their entire nation of able fighters amounts only to a dozen or so large commanderies of China.
translations.idiomatic: Among the four barbarians, the strongest and greatest threat to China is none greater than Tibet—their entire nation of able fighters amounts only to a dozen or so large commanderies of China.

sentences.zh: 其於內虞外備，亦與中國不殊，所能寇邊，數則蓋寡。

translations.literal: In internal worries and external defenses they differ little from China; the forces they can send to raid the border are in number surely few.
translations.idiomatic: In internal worries and external defenses they differ little from China; the forces they can send to raid the border are surely few in number.

sentences.zh: 且又器非犀利，甲不堅完，識迷韜鈐，藝乏趫敏。

translations.literal: Moreover their weapons are not sharp, their armor not solid and complete; their understanding of military arts is confused, their skills lack agility.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover their weapons are not sharp, their armor not solid and complete; their understanding of military arts is confused, their skills lack agility.

sentences.zh: 動則中國畏其眾而不敢抗，靜則中國憚其強而不敢侵，厥理何哉？

translations.literal: When they move, China fears their numbers and dares not resist; when they rest, China dreads their strength and dares not attack—what is the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: When they move, China fears their numbers and dares not resist; when they rest, China dreads their strength and dares not attack—what is the reason for this?

sentences.zh: 良以中國之節制多門，蕃醜之統帥專一故也。

translations.literal: Truly because China's command structure has many gates, while the barbarian chieftains' command is unified.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because China's command structure has many gates, while the barbarian chieftains' command is unified.

sentences.zh: 夫統帥專則人心不分，人心不分則號令不貳，號令不貳則進退可齊，進退可齊則疾徐如意，疾徐如意則機會靡愆，機會靡愆則氣勢自壯！

translations.literal: When command is unified, hearts are not divided; when hearts are not divided, orders are not twofold; when orders are not twofold, advance and retreat can be aligned; when advance and retreat can be aligned, speed and pause obey the will; when speed and pause obey the will, opportunities are not missed; when opportunities are not missed, martial spirit naturally grows strong!
translations.idiomatic: When command is unified, hearts are not divided; when hearts are not divided, orders are not twofold; when orders are not twofold, advance and retreat can be aligned; when advance and retreat can be aligned, speed and pause obey the will; when speed and pause obey the will, opportunities are not missed; when opportunities are not missed, martial spirit naturally grows strong!

sentences.zh: 斯乃以少為眾，以弱為強，變化翕辟，在於反掌之內。

translations.literal: Thus with few they become many, with weak they become strong; transformation expanding and contracting lies within the turn of the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus with few they become many, with weak they become strong; transformation expanding and contracting lies within the turn of the palm.

sentences.zh: 是猶臂之使指，心之制形，若所任得人，則何敵之有！

translations.literal: It is like the arm commanding the fingers, the heart governing the body—if the right men are appointed, what enemy could there be!
translations.idiomatic: It is like the arm commanding the fingers, the heart governing the body—if the right men are appointed, what enemy could there be!

sentences.zh: 夫節制多門則人心不一，人心不一則號令不行，號令不行則進退難必，進退難必則疾徐失宜，疾徐失宜則機會不及，機會不及則氣勢自衰！

translations.literal: When command has many gates, hearts are not united; when hearts are not united, orders are not carried out; when orders are not carried out, advance and retreat cannot be assured; when advance and retreat cannot be assured, speed and pause fall out of alignment; when speed and pause fall out of alignment, opportunities are not seized; when opportunities are not seized, martial spirit naturally wanes!
translations.idiomatic: When command has many gates, hearts are not united; when hearts are not united, orders are not carried out; when orders are not carried out, advance and retreat cannot be assured; when advance and retreat cannot be assured, speed and pause fall out of alignment; when speed and pause fall out of alignment, opportunities are not seized; when opportunities are not seized, martial spirit naturally wanes!

sentences.zh: 斯乃勇廢為尪，眾散為弱，逗撓離析，兆乎戰陣之前。

translations.literal: Thus courage collapses into weakness, the multitude scatters into feebleness—hesitation and dissolution show themselves before the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Thus courage collapses into weakness, the multitude scatters into feebleness—hesitation and dissolution show themselves before the battle line.

sentences.zh: 是猶一國三公，十羊九牧，欲令齊肅，其可得乎？

translations.literal: It is like three dukes in one state, nine herdsmen for ten sheep—wishing to make them uniformly disciplined, how could it be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: It is like three dukes in one state, nine herdsmen for ten sheep—wishing to make them uniformly disciplined, how could it be achieved?

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶之間，控禦西北兩蕃，唯朔方、河西、隴右三節度而已，猶慮權分勢散，或使兼而領之。

translations.literal: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, controlling the two fan peoples of the northwest required only the three frontier commissions of Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou—and even then there was concern that divided authority would scatter strength, so sometimes one man was made to command them jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, controlling the two northwestern barbarian peoples required only the three frontier commissions of Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou—and even then there was concern that divided authority would scatter strength, so sometimes one man was made to command them jointly.

sentences.zh: 中興已來，未遑外討，僑隸四鎮於安定，權附隴右於扶風，所當西北兩蕃，亦朔方、涇原、隴右、河東節度而已，關東戍卒，至則屬焉。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, with no leisure for external campaigns, the Four Garrisons were provisionally attached at Anding and Longyou provisionally subordinated at Fufeng—against the two northwestern fan peoples there were again only the Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong commissions; garrison soldiers from east of the pass, when they arrived, fell under their authority.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration, with no leisure for external campaigns, the Four Garrisons were provisionally attached at Anding and Longyou provisionally subordinated at Fufeng. Against the two northwestern barbarian peoples there were again only the Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong commissions; garrison soldiers from east of the pass, when they arrived, fell under their authority.

sentences.zh: 雖委任未盡得人，而措置尚存典制。

translations.literal: Though appointments did not always find the right men, the arrangements still preserved the proper institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Though appointments did not always find the right men, the arrangements still preserved the proper institutions.

sentences.zh: 自頃逆泚誘涇、隴之眾叛，懷光汙朔方之軍，割裂誅鋤，所余無幾。

translations.literal: Recently the rebel Zhu Ci induced the armies of Jing and Long to defect; Huai'guang corrupted the Shuofang army—after partition and purges, little remained.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the rebel Zhu Ci induced the armies of Jing and Long to defect; Huai'guang corrupted the Shuofang army—after partition and purges, little remained.

sentences.zh: 而又分朔方之地，建牙擁節者，凡三使焉。

translations.literal: Moreover Shuofang's territory was divided—those who established headquarters and bore commander's staffs numbered three in all.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shuofang's territory was divided—those who established headquarters and bore commander's staffs numbered three in all.

sentences.zh: 其余鎮軍，數且四十，皆承特詔委寄，各降中貴監臨，人得抗衡，莫相稟屬。

translations.literal: The remaining garrison armies number nearly forty—all commissioned by special edict, each supervised by a palace eunuch envoy; men are equals to one another, none subordinate to another.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining garrison armies number nearly forty—all commissioned by special edict, each supervised by a palace eunuch envoy; men are equals to one another, none subordinate to another.

sentences.zh: 每俟邊書告急，方令計會用兵，既無軍法下臨，唯以客禮相待。

translations.literal: Only when frontier dispatches report emergency are orders given to coordinate troops—and with no military law descending from above, they are treated only with the courtesy due guests.
translations.idiomatic: Only when frontier dispatches report emergency are orders given to coordinate troops—and with no military law descending from above, they are treated only with the courtesy due guests.

sentences.zh: 是乃從容拯溺，揖讓救焚，冀無阽危，固亦難矣！

translations.literal: This is to save the drowning at leisure and fight the fire with bows and courtesies—to hope for no peril on the brink, how difficult that surely is!
translations.idiomatic: This is to save the drowning at leisure and fight the fire with bows and courtesies—to hope for no peril on the brink, how difficult that surely is!

sentences.zh: 夫兵，以氣勢為用者也，氣聚則盛，散則消；

translations.literal: Warfare relies on martial spirit—when spirit gathers it flourishes, when it scatters it dissipates;
translations.idiomatic: Warfare relies on martial spirit—when spirit gathers it flourishes, when it scatters it dissipates;

sentences.zh: 勢合則威，析則弱。

translations.literal: When force combines it is formidable, when divided it is weak.
translations.idiomatic: When force combines it is formidable, when divided it is weak.

sentences.zh: 今之邊備，勢弱氣消，建軍若斯，可謂力分於將多矣。

translations.literal: Today's border defenses—weak in force, dissipated in spirit—to establish armies thus may be called strength divided among too many generals!
translations.idiomatic: Today's border defenses are weak in force and dissipated in spirit—to establish armies thus is what I call strength divided among too many generals!

sentences.zh: 理戎之要，最在均齊，故軍法無貴賤之差，軍實無多少之異，是將所以同其誌而盡其力也。

translations.literal: The crux of managing the frontier lies above all in equality and balance—thus military law makes no distinction of high and low rank, military provisions no difference of more and less—this is how generals unite men's resolve and exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The crux of managing the frontier lies above all in equality and balance—thus military law makes no distinction of high and low rank, military provisions no difference of more and less. This is how generals unite men's resolve and exhaust their strength.

sentences.zh: 如或誘其誌意，勉其藝能，則當閱其材，程其勇，校其勞逸，度其安危，明申練覆優劣之科，以為衣食等級之制。

translations.literal: If one would draw out their resolve and encourage their skills, one should assess their talent, measure their courage, compare their toil and rest, gauge their peril and safety—clearly establishing categories for training review and merit, to serve as the system of graded food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: If one would draw out their resolve and encourage their skills, one should assess their talent, measure their courage, compare their toil and rest, gauge their peril and safety—clearly establishing categories for training review and merit, to serve as the system of graded food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 使能者企及，否者息心，雖有薄厚之殊，而無觖望之釁。

translations.literal: Let the capable strive to catch up, the incapable lay aside ambition—though there be differences of more and less, there will be no cause for discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Let the capable strive to catch up, the incapable lay aside ambition—though there be differences of more and less, there will be no cause for discontent.

sentences.zh: 蓋所謂日省月試，餼稟均事，如權量之無情於物，萬人莫不安其分而服其平也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by daily review and monthly testing, rations distributed with equal fairness—like the balance scale indifferent to objects; ten thousand men none failing to rest content in their station and submit to its fairness.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by daily review and monthly testing, rations distributed with equal fairness—like the balance scale indifferent to objects; ten thousand men none failing to rest content in their station and submit to its fairness.

sentences.zh: 今者窮邊之地，長鎮之兵，皆百戰傷夷之余，終年勤苦之劇，角其所能則練習，度其所處則孤危，考其服役則勞，察其臨敵則勇。

translations.literal: Now on the remote frontier, the long-garrisoned troops—all are survivors of a hundred battles and wounds, enduring year-round the severest toil; matched against their abilities they are practiced, measured against their situation they stand alone and in peril, examined for their service they are worn with labor, observed facing the enemy they are brave.
translations.idiomatic: Now on the remote frontier, the long-garrisoned troops are all survivors of a hundred battles and wounds, enduring year-round the severest toil. Matched against their abilities they are practiced; measured against their situation they stand alone and in peril; examined for their service they are worn with labor; observed facing the enemy they are brave.

sentences.zh: 然衣糧所給，唯止當身，例為妻子所分，常有凍餒之色。

translations.literal: Yet the clothing and grain provided reach only their own bodies, and as a rule are divided among wives and children—they constantly wear the look of cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the clothing and grain provided reach only their own bodies, and as a rule are divided among wives and children—they constantly wear the look of cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 而關東戍卒，歲月踐更，不安危城，不習戎備，怯於應敵，懈於服勞。

translations.literal: Yet garrison soldiers from east of the pass, rotating through by month and year, untested in perilous fortresses, unpracticed in military readiness, timid in facing the enemy, slack in bearing labor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet garrison soldiers from east of the pass, rotating through by month and year, are untested in perilous fortresses, unpracticed in military readiness, timid in facing the enemy, and slack in bearing labor.

sentences.zh: 然衣糧所頒，厚逾數等，繼以茶藥之饋，益以蔬醬之資。

translations.literal: Yet the clothing and grain they receive is generous by several grades, followed by gifts of tea and medicine, supplemented with vegetables and sauces.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the clothing and grain they receive is generous by several grades, followed by gifts of tea and medicine, supplemented with vegetables and sauces.

sentences.zh: 豐約相形，懸絕斯甚。

translations.literal: Abundance and want set side by side—the gap is vast.
translations.idiomatic: Abundance and want set side by side—the gap is vast.

sentences.zh: 又有素非禁旅，本是邊軍，將校詭為媚詞，因請遙隸神策，不離舊所，唯改虛名，其於稟賜之饒，遂有三倍之益。

translations.literal: There are also men who were never of the imperial guard but were originally frontier troops—officers craftily using flattery petition to be nominally attached to the Shence Army from afar, never leaving their old posts, changing only an empty title—yet their rations and gifts become three times richer.
translations.idiomatic: There are also men who were never of the imperial guard but were originally frontier troops—officers craftily using flattery petition to be nominally attached to the Shence Army from afar, never leaving their old posts, changing only an empty title—yet their rations and gifts become three times richer.

sentences.zh: 此儔類所以忿恨，忠良所以憂嗟，疲人所以流亡，經費所以褊匱。

translations.literal: This is why such comrades boil with resentment, loyal men sigh with worry, the worn-out flee into exile, and military funds run thin.
translations.idiomatic: This is why such comrades boil with resentment, loyal men sigh with worry, the worn-out flee into exile, and military funds run thin.

sentences.zh: 夫事業未異，而給養有殊，人情之所不能甘也，況乎矯佞行而稟賜厚，績藝劣而衣食優，茍未忘懷，能無慍怒！

translations.literal: When the service is no different yet sustenance is unequal—this human nature cannot accept; how much less when sycophancy wins rich rations while poor merit receives fine food and clothing—if one has not forgotten self, how could there be no anger!
translations.idiomatic: When the service is no different yet sustenance is unequal—this human nature cannot accept. How much less when sycophancy wins rich rations while poor merit receives fine food and clothing—if one has not forgotten self, how could there be no anger!

sentences.zh: 不為戎首，則已可嘉，而欲使其協力同心，以攘寇難，雖有韓、白、孫、吳之將，臣知其必不能焉。

translations.literal: For them not to lead the barbarians' charge would already be praiseworthy—and to expect them to unite in heart and strength to repel the enemy, even with generals like Han Xin, Bai Qi, Sun Wu, and Wu Qi, I know it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: For them not to lead the barbarians' charge would already be praiseworthy—and to expect them to unite in heart and strength to repel the enemy, even with generals like Han Xin, Bai Qi, Sun Wu, and Wu Qi, I know it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 養士若斯，可謂怨生於不均矣！

translations.literal: To sustain troops thus may be called resentment born of inequality!
translations.idiomatic: To sustain troops thus is what I call resentment born of inequality!

sentences.zh: 凡欲選任將帥，必先考察行能，然後指以所授之方，語以所委之事，令其自揣可否，自陳規模。

translations.literal: Whenever one wishes to select and appoint generals, one must first examine conduct and ability, then point out the region to be entrusted and explain the duties assigned, letting them judge for themselves whether they can do it and state their own plans.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever one wishes to select and appoint generals, one must first examine conduct and ability, then point out the region to be entrusted and explain the duties assigned, letting them judge for themselves whether they can do it and state their own plans.

sentences.zh: 須某色甲兵，藉某人參佐，要若干士馬，用若干資糧，某處置軍，某時成績，始終要領，悉俾經綸，於是觀其計謀，校其聲實。

translations.literal: One must specify what kind of armor and troops are needed, whom to rely on as aides, how many soldiers and horses are required, how much provisions and grain to use, where to deploy the army, when results are expected—the essentials from start to finish all entrusted to their planning—then observe their stratagems and weigh name against reality.
translations.idiomatic: Specify the armor and troops required, the aides to be relied upon, the number of soldiers and horses needed, the provisions and grain to be supplied, where to deploy the army, and when results are expected. Entrust the essentials from start to finish to their planning, then observe their stratagems and weigh name against reality.

sentences.zh: 若謂材無足取，言不可行，則當退之於初，不宜貽慮於其後也。

translations.literal: If one holds that his talent is not worth taking and his words cannot be carried out, then he should be dismissed at the outset—not left with concerns afterward.
translations.idiomatic: If his talent is deemed unworthy and his proposals unworkable, dismiss him at the outset; do not let doubts linger afterward.

sentences.zh: 若謂志氣足任，方略可施，則當要之於終，不宜掣肘於其間也。

translations.literal: If one holds that his resolve is sufficient for the task and his strategy can be applied, then he should be held to the end—not hamstrung in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: If his resolve is judged sufficient and his strategy workable, hold him to the end; do not hamstring him midway.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則疑者不使，使者不疑；

translations.literal: If so, the doubtful are not employed, and those employed are not doubted;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the doubtful are not employed, and those employed are not doubted;

sentences.zh: 勞神於選才，端拱於委任。

translations.literal: One strains the mind in selecting talent and sits upright in dignified repose to delegate authority.
translations.idiomatic: Exert effort only in selecting talent, then sit back in dignified repose to delegate authority.

sentences.zh: 既委其事，既足其求，然後可以核其否臧，行其賞罰。

translations.literal: Once the task is entrusted and their requests are fully met, then one may examine success or failure and apply rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Once the task is entrusted and their requests fully met, then one may judge success or failure and apply rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 受賞者不以為濫，當罰者無得而辭，付授之柄既專，茍且之心自息。

translations.literal: Those rewarded will not call it excessive; those who deserve punishment have no excuse—the delegated authority being complete, the spirit of temporizing naturally subsides.
translations.idiomatic: The rewarded will not deem it excessive; the deserving of punishment will have no recourse. With authority fully delegated, the impulse to cut corners naturally dies away.

sentences.zh: 是以古之遣將帥者，君親推轂而命之曰：「自閫以外，將軍裁之。」

translations.literal: Hence when ancient rulers dispatched generals, the ruler in person pushed the chariot wheel and commanded: "Beyond the frontier gate, the general decides."
translations.idiomatic: Hence when ancient rulers dispatched generals, the ruler in person would push the chariot wheel and say: "Beyond the frontier gate, the general decides.

sentences.zh: 又賜鈇鉞，示令專斷。

translations.literal: He also bestowed the axe and halberd, signaling authority for independent judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed the axe and halberd, signaling authority for independent judgment.

sentences.zh: 故軍容不入國，國容不入軍，將在軍，君命有所不受。

translations.literal: Thus military etiquette does not enter the state, and state etiquette does not enter the army; when the general is in the army, the ruler's orders may sometimes go unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Thus military protocol does not enter the court, nor court protocol the army. When the general is in the field, he may sometimes refuse the ruler's orders.

sentences.zh: 誠謂機宜不可以遠決，號令不可以兩從，未有委任不專，而望其克敵成功者也。

translations.literal: Truly, opportune action cannot be decided from afar, commands cannot have two masters; never has there been one whose delegation was not complete yet who was expected to defeat the enemy and succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Truly, opportune action cannot be decided from afar, nor commands obey two masters. No one whose authority was divided has ever been expected to defeat the enemy and succeed.

sentences.zh: 自頃邊軍去就，裁斷多出宸衷，選置戎臣，先求易制，多其部以分其力，輕其任以弱其心，雖有所懲，亦有所失。

translations.literal: Recently the border armies' movements and deployments have mostly been decided from the imperial heart; in selecting military officials, easy control is sought first—giving them many subordinates to divide their strength, lightening their duties to weaken their resolve—though some gain is had, some is also lost.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the border armies' movements have mostly been decided from the throne itself. In appointing military officials, easy control comes first: many subordinates to divide their strength, lighter duties to weaken their resolve. Though some good may come of this, much is also lost.

sentences.zh: 遂令分閫責成之義廢，死綏任咎之誌衰，一則聽命，二亦聽命，爽於軍情亦聽命，乖於事宜亦聽命。

translations.literal: Thus the principle of entrusting a sector with responsibility is abandoned, the resolve to die at one's post and bear blame fades—first one listens to orders, second also listens to orders; at odds with military conditions also listens to orders, contrary to what the situation requires also listens to orders.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the principle of entrusting a sector with full responsibility is abandoned, and the resolve to die at one's post and bear blame fades. First one takes orders, then another takes orders; at odds with military conditions—take orders; contrary to the situation—take orders.

sentences.zh: 若所置將帥，必取於承順無違，則如斯可矣；

translations.literal: If the generals appointed must be drawn from those who comply without dissent, then such a course would do;
translations.idiomatic: If the generals appointed must be those who comply without dissent, then such a course might suffice;

sentences.zh: 若有意平兇靖難，則不可。

translations.literal: If one intends to pacify the violent and settle turmoil, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: But if one intends to pacify the violent and settle turmoil, it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 夫兩境相接，兩軍相持，事機之來，間不容息，蓄謀而俟，猶恐失之，臨時始謀，固已疏矣。

translations.literal: When two borders meet and two armies face each other, opportunity arrives allowing no pause for breath—even storing plans and waiting, one still fears missing it; to plan only when the moment comes is already too lax.
translations.idiomatic: When two borders meet and two armies face each other, opportunity brooks no pause—even plans prepared in advance may still be missed; to plan only when crisis strikes is already far too late.

sentences.zh: 況乎千里之遠，九重之深，陳述之難明，聽覽之不一，欲其事無遺策，雖聖者亦有所不能焉。

translations.literal: How much more when a thousand li lie between, and the ninefold palace is deep—the difficulty of making matters clear in reports, the inconsistency of imperial attention—to wish that nothing be overlooked, even a sage has what he cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when a thousand li lie between and the palace depths are impenetrable—reports hard to make clear, imperial attention inconsistent. To expect that nothing be overlooked is beyond even a sage.

sentences.zh: 設使謀慮能周，其如權變無及！

translations.literal: Even if deliberation could be thorough, what of timely adaptation when there is no time!
translations.idiomatic: Even if deliberation could be thorough, what of timely adaptation when there is no time!

sentences.zh: 戎虜馳突，迅如風飈，驛書上聞，旬月方報。

translations.literal: The barbarian foe charges swiftly, quick as a wind-gust; memorials by post reach the throne, and a reply comes only after ten days or a month.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian foe charges as swiftly as a wind-gust. Memorials by post reach the throne, and a reply may come only after ten days or a month.

sentences.zh: 守土者以兵寡不敢抗敵，分鎮者以無詔不肯出師，逗留之間，寇已奔逼，托於救援未至，各且閉壘自全。

translations.literal: Territory defenders, finding their troops few, dare not resist the enemy; sector commanders, lacking an edict, refuse to march out; in the delay the bandits are already upon them—pleading that relief has not arrived, each closes his fortress to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Local defenders, finding their troops too few, dare not resist. Sector commanders, lacking an edict, refuse to march out. While they delay, the raiders are already upon them. Pleading that relief has not arrived, each closes his fort and saves himself.

sentences.zh: 牧馬屯牛，鞠為椎剽；

translations.literal: Pastured horses and penned cattle become fodder for raids;
translations.idiomatic: Horses in pasture and cattle in pens become the spoil of raids;

sentences.zh: 穡夫樵婦，罄作俘囚。

translations.literal: Farmers and wood-gathering women, all become captives.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers and wood-gathering women are taken wholesale as captives.

sentences.zh: 雖詔諸鎮發兵，唯以虛聲應援，互相瞻顧，莫敢遮邀，賊既縱掠退歸，此乃陳功告捷。

translations.literal: Although edicts order the various sectors to send troops, they respond with only an empty sound of support, eyeing one another, none daring to intercept and engage; once the bandits have finished plundering and withdrawn, only then do they report merit and proclaim victory.
translations.idiomatic: Though edicts order the various sectors to mobilize, they respond with only a hollow show of support, watching one another, none daring to intercept the enemy. Once the raiders have finished plundering and withdrawn, they report merit and proclaim victory.

sentences.zh: 其敗喪則減百而為一，其捃獲則張百而成千。

translations.literal: Their defeats and losses are reduced from a hundred to one; their gathered booty is inflated from a hundred to a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Defeats and losses are reported at one-hundredth of their true scale; booty seized is inflated from hundreds into thousands.

sentences.zh: 將帥既幸於總制在朝，不憂於罪累；

translations.literal: The generals, fortunate that overall control rests at court, need not worry about guilt and punishment;
translations.idiomatic: The generals, fortunate that overall control rests at court, need not fear blame;

sentences.zh: 陛下又以為大權由己，不究事情。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also, believing that supreme authority rests with yourself, does not investigate the actual facts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, believing supreme authority rests with yourself, does not investigate the actual facts.

sentences.zh: 用師若斯，可謂機失於遙制矣！

translations.literal: To use troops thus may be called losing opportunity through remote control!
translations.idiomatic: To use troops thus is what I call losing opportunity through remote control!

sentences.zh: 理兵而措置乖方，馭將而賞罰虧度，制用而財匱，建兵而力分，養士而怨生，用師而機失，此六者，疆場之蟊賊，軍旅之膏肓也。

translations.literal: Deploying troops with misplaced arrangements, governing generals with deficient rewards and punishments, controlling expenditures until funds run short, raising armies while strength is divided, sustaining soldiers until resentment arises, using troops while opportunity is lost—these six are the crop pests of the frontier and the deep ailment of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Deploying troops with misplaced arrangements, governing generals with deficient rewards and punishments, controlling expenditures until funds run short, raising armies while strength is divided, sustaining soldiers until resentment arises, using troops while opportunity is lost—these six are the crop pests of the frontier and the deep-rooted ailment of the army.

sentences.zh: 蟊賊不除，而但滋之以糞溉，膏肓不療，而唯啖之以滑甘，適足以養其害，速其災，欲求稼穡豐登，膚革充美，固不可得也。

translations.literal: If crop pests are not removed but only nourished with manure and water, if the deep ailment is not treated but only fed sweet and slick things, this merely nurtures the harm and hastens disaster—to hope for rich harvests and full, healthy flesh is surely unattainable.
translations.idiomatic: If crop pests are not removed but only fed with fertilizer, if the deep ailment is not treated but only pampered with sweet delicacies, this merely nurtures the harm and hastens disaster. To hope for rich harvests and a strong, healthy people is surely impossible.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂宜罷諸道將士番替防秋之制，率因舊數而三分之：其一分委本道節度使募少壯願住邊城者以徙焉；

translations.literal: Your humble servant holds that the system of rotating troops from all circuits for autumn border defense should be abolished, and the old quotas divided roughly into three parts: one part left to the circuit military commissioner to recruit young, strong men willing to dwell in border towns for resettlement there;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the system of rotating troops from all circuits for autumn border defense should be abolished, and the existing quotas divided into three. One part should be entrusted to each circuit's military commissioner to recruit able-bodied young men willing to settle in border towns.

sentences.zh: 其一分則本道但供衣糧，委關內、河東諸軍州募蕃、漢子弟願傅邊軍者以給焉；

translations.literal: One part with the circuit supplying only clothing and grain, entrusting the districts and armies within the passes and in Hedong to recruit tribal and Han youth willing to serve with the border army;
translations.idiomatic: For another part, the circuit would supply only clothing and grain, while districts and armies within the passes and in Hedong would recruit tribal and Han youth willing to join the border forces.

sentences.zh: 又一分亦令本道但出衣糧，加給應募之人，以資新徙之業。

translations.literal: Another part likewise having the circuit provide only clothing and grain, with additional pay to those who enlist, to support the livelihood of the newly resettled.
translations.idiomatic: For a third part, the circuit would again supply only clothing and grain, with extra pay to recruits to support the livelihood of the newly resettled.

sentences.zh: 又令度支散於諸道和市耕牛，兼雇召工人，就諸軍城繕造器具。

translations.literal: Further, order the Office of Revenue to disperse through the circuits to purchase plow oxen, and also hire workers to repair and make implements at the various military posts.
translations.idiomatic: Further, the Office of Revenue should purchase plow oxen throughout the circuits and hire workers to make and repair implements at the various military posts.

sentences.zh: 募人至者，每家給耕牛一頭，又給田農水火之器，皆令充備。

translations.literal: When recruits arrive, each household should be given one plow ox, and also farming tools for field, fire, and water—all made fully sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: When recruits arrive, each household should receive one plow ox and a full set of farming implements for field work and household use.

sentences.zh: 初到之歲，與家口二人糧，並賜種子，勸之播植，待經一稔，俾自給家。

translations.literal: In the first year of arrival, provide grain for two family members, and also grant seed, encouraging them to sow and plant; after one harvest, let them support their own households.
translations.idiomatic: In their first year, provide grain for two family members and grant seed, encouraging them to plant. After one harvest, they should be able to support their own households.

sentences.zh: 若有余糧，官為收糴，各酬倍價，務獎營田。

translations.literal: If there is surplus grain, the government should purchase it, paying double the price, vigorously encouraging border farming.
translations.idiomatic: If there is surplus grain, the government should buy it at double the market price, vigorously encouraging border farming.

sentences.zh: 既息踐更征發之煩，且無幸災茍免之弊。

translations.literal: This both ends the troubles of rotating service and levy, and removes the abuse of hoping for disaster to escape duty.
translations.idiomatic: This would end the troubles of rotating service and conscription, and remove the abuse of hoping for disaster as a way to escape duty.

sentences.zh: 寇至則人自為戰，時至則家自力農。

translations.literal: When bandits come, each man fights on his own; when the season comes, each household farms on its own.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders come, each man will fight on his own; when the season comes, each household will farm on its own.

sentences.zh: 是乃兵不得不強，食不得不足，與夫倏來忽往，豈可同等而論哉！

translations.literal: Thus troops cannot but be strong, food cannot but be sufficient—compared with those who come suddenly and go suddenly, how can they be spoken of on equal terms!
translations.idiomatic: Thus the army must grow strong and provisions must suffice—how can this be compared with troops who come suddenly and depart just as quickly!

sentences.zh: 臣又謂宜擇文武能臣一人為隴右元帥，應涇、隴、鳳翔、長武城、山南西道等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；

translations.literal: Your servant further holds that one capable civil and military official should be chosen as Commander of the Right of Longyou, and all troops within the jurisdictions of the Jing, Long, Fengxiang, Changwucheng, and Shannan West circuit commands should be placed under him;
translations.idiomatic: I further hold that one capable civil and military official should be chosen as Commander of the Right of Longyou, placing all troops under the Jing, Long, Fengxiang, Changwucheng, and Shannan West circuit commands under his authority.

sentences.zh: 又擇一人為朔方元帥，應鄜坊、邠寧、靈夏等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；

translations.literal: Choose another as Commander of Shuofang, and all troops within the Fufang, Binning, Lingxia, and related circuit commands should be placed under him;
translations.idiomatic: Choose another as Commander of Shuofang, placing all troops under the Fufang, Binning, Lingxia, and related commands under his authority.

sentences.zh: 又擇一人為河東元帥，河東、振武等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉。

translations.literal: Choose another as Commander of Hedong, and all troops within the Hedong and Zhenwu circuit commands should be placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Choose another as Commander of Hedong, placing all troops under the Hedong and Zhenwu commands under his authority.

sentences.zh: 三帥各選臨邊要會之州以為理所，見置節度，有非要者，隨所便近而並之。

translations.literal: Each of the three commanders should choose a strategic border prefecture as his headquarters; among existing military commissions, those not essential should be merged according to convenience and proximity.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three commanders should establish headquarters at a strategic border prefecture. Among existing military commissions, nonessential ones should be merged according to convenience and proximity.

sentences.zh: 唯元帥得置統軍，余並停罷。

translations.literal: Only the commanders-in-chief may appoint army overseers; all others should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Only the commanders-in-chief may appoint army overseers; all other such posts should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 其三帥部內太原、鳳翔等府及諸郡戶口稍多者，慎揀良吏以為尹守，外奉師律，內課農桑，俾為軍糧，以壯戎府。

translations.literal: Within the three commanders' territories, for Taiyuan, Fengxiang, and other prefectures and commanderies with relatively large populations, carefully select good officials as governors and prefects—outwardly observing military discipline, inwardly encouraging agriculture and sericulture, making them sources of army grain to strengthen the military posts.
translations.idiomatic: Within the three commanders' territories, for Taiyuan, Fengxiang, and other prefectures with relatively large populations, carefully select good officials as governors. Outwardly they should observe military discipline; inwardly they should encourage agriculture and sericulture, supplying army grain to strengthen the military posts.

sentences.zh: 理兵之宜既得，選帥之授既明，然後減奸濫虛浮之費以豐財，定衣糧等級之制以和眾，弘委任之道以宣其用，懸賞罰之典以考其成。

translations.literal: Once the right way to deploy troops is settled and the appointment of commanders is clear, then reduce corrupt, excessive, and empty expenditures to enrich the treasury, fix grades for clothing and grain to harmonize the ranks, broaden the way of delegation to display their usefulness, and publish standards of reward and punishment to assess their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Once troop deployment is rightly ordered and commanders clearly appointed, reduce corrupt and wasteful expenditures to enrich the treasury, fix grades for clothing and grain to harmonize the ranks, broaden delegation to put talent to use, and publish standards of reward and punishment to assess achievement.

sentences.zh: 而又慎守中國之所長，謹行當今之所易，則八利可致，六失可除。

translations.literal: Moreover, carefully hold to what China excels at, and diligently practice what is easy in the present day—then the eight benefits can be attained and the six failures removed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, carefully hold to China's strengths and diligently practice what is feasible today, and the eight benefits can be attained and the six failures removed.

sentences.zh: 如是而戎狄不威懷，疆場不寧謐者，未之有也。

translations.literal: If this is done yet the barbarians are neither awed nor won over, and the frontier is not settled and quiet—never has such a thing been.
translations.idiomatic: If this is done and yet the barbarians are neither awed nor reconciled, and the frontier is not settled—there has never been such a case.

sentences.zh: 諸侯軌道，庶類服從。

translations.literal: The feudal lords would follow the correct path, and the common folk would submit.
translations.idiomatic: The regional lords would follow the correct path, and the people would submit.

sentences.zh: 如是而教令不行，天下不理者，亦未之有也。

translations.literal: If this is done yet edicts and orders do not prevail and the realm is not well governed—never has such a thing been either.
translations.idiomatic: If this is done and yet edicts do not prevail and the realm is not well governed—that too has never happened.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之英鑒，民心之思安，四方之小休，兩寇之方靜，加以頻年豐稔，所在積糧，此皆天贊國家，可以立制垂統之時也。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's keen insight, the people's wish for peace, a brief rest in the four quarters, the two enemy peoples just settling down, plus years of abundant harvests and grain stored everywhere—all this is Heaven aiding the state; it is a time to establish institutions and leave a lasting legacy.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's keen insight, the people's longing for peace, a brief respite in the four quarters, the two enemy peoples just quieting down, and years of abundant harvest with grain stored everywhere—all this is Heaven aiding the state. It is a time to establish institutions and leave a lasting legacy.

sentences.zh: 時不久居，事不常兼，已過而追，雖悔無及。

translations.literal: Time does not long remain, affairs do not usually coincide; once passed and pursued, though one regrets, it is too late.
translations.idiomatic: Time does not long remain, and favorable conditions do not often coincide. Once the moment has passed, regret comes too late.

sentences.zh: 明主者，不以言為罪，不以人廢言，罄陳狂愚，惟所省擇。

translations.literal: A wise ruler does not punish for words spoken, does not discard words because of the speaker—I lay out my foolishness fully and leave all to Your careful choice.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler does not punish for words spoken or discard counsel because of the speaker. I lay out my foolishness fully and leave all to Your careful judgment.

sentences.zh: 德宗極深嘉納，優詔褒獎之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong greatly approved and accepted it, issuing a gracious edict to praise and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong greatly approved and accepted the memorial, issuing a gracious edict to praise and reward him.

sentences.zh: 贄在中書，政不便於時者，多所條奏。

translations.literal: While Zhi was at the Secretariat, on matters of government ill-suited to the times he submitted many detailed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhi served at the Secretariat, he submitted many detailed memorials on matters of government ill-suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 德宗雖不能皆可，而心頗重之。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Dezong could not approve them all, in his heart he highly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Dezong could not approve them all, he highly valued him at heart.

sentences.zh: 初，竇參既貶郴州，節度使劉士寧餉參絹數千匹。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Dou Can was demoted to Chenzhou, Military Commissioner Liu Shining sent Can several thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Dou Can was demoted to Chenzhou, Military Commissioner Liu Shining sent him several thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使李巽與參有隙，具事奏聞，德宗不悅。

translations.literal: Hunan Observation Commissioner Li Xun had a grudge against Can and reported the full matter to the throne; Emperor Dezong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Observation Commissioner Li Xun, who bore a grudge against Can, reported the full matter to the throne. Emperor Dezong was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會右庶子姜公輔於上前聞奏，稱「竇參嘗語臣云：陛下怒臣未已」，德宗怒，再貶參，竟殺之。

translations.literal: It happened that Right Counseled Instructor Jiang Gongfu heard the report before the throne and stated, "Dou Can once told me: 'Your Majesty's anger at me is not yet spent'"—Emperor Dezong grew angry, demoted Can again, and ultimately had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Right Counseled Instructor Jiang Gongfu heard the report at court and said, "Dou Can once told me, 'Your Majesty's anger at me is not yet spent.'" Emperor Dezong grew angry, demoted Can again, and ultimately had him executed.

sentences.zh: 時議雲公輔奏竇參語得之於贄，雲參之死，贄有力焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that Gongfu's report of Dou Can's words came from Zhi, and that Zhi had a hand in Can's death.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that Gongfu's report of Dou Can's words came from Zhi, and that Zhi had a hand in Can's death.

sentences.zh: 又素惡於公異、於邵，既輔政而逐之，談者亦以為厄。

translations.literal: He had also long been at odds with Gong Yi and Yu Shao; once he became chief minister he drove them out—and gossips likewise regarded this as an ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: He had also long been at odds with Gong Yi and Yu Shao; once he became chief minister he drove them out, and gossips likewise regarded this as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎、判度支裴延齡，奸宄用事，天下嫉之如仇。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Director of the Office of Revenue Pei Yanling, a villain in power, was hated throughout the realm like a mortal enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Director of the Office of Revenue Pei Yanling, a villain in power, was hated throughout the realm like a mortal enemy.

sentences.zh: 以得幸於天子，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Because he had won the Son of Heaven's favor, no one dared speak against him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had won the emperor's favor, no one dared speak against him.

sentences.zh: 贄獨以身當之，屢於延英面陳其不可，累上疏極言其弊。

translations.literal: Zhi alone put himself in the breach, repeatedly stating face to face in the Yanying Hall that Yanling's course was wrong, and submitting memorial after memorial forcefully declaring his abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi alone stood in the breach, repeatedly arguing face to face in the Yanying Hall that Yanling's course was wrong, and submitting memorial after memorial forcefully declaring his abuses.

sentences.zh: 延齡日加譖毀。

translations.literal: Yanling daily increased his slander.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling daily increased his slander against him.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，除太子賓客，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, he was appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent and dismissed from participating in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the tenth year of the Zhenyuan reign, he was appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent and dismissed from participating in governance.

sentences.zh: 贄性畏慎，及策免私居，朝謁之外，不通賓客，無所過從。

translations.literal: Zhi by nature was cautious and timid; once dismissed and living privately, beyond attending court audiences he received no guests and kept no company.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was cautious by nature. Once dismissed and living in private retirement, beyond attending court audiences he received no guests and kept no company.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，旱，邊軍芻粟不給，具事論訴；

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, drought struck; the border armies lacked fodder and grain, and they petitioned with full accounts of their grievances;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, drought struck. The border armies lacked fodder and grain and petitioned with full accounts of their grievances.

sentences.zh: 延齡言贄與張滂、李充等搖動軍情，語在《延齡傳》。

translations.literal: Yanling claimed that Zhi, together with Zhang Pang, Li Chong, and others, had stirred up military sentiment—the account is in the Biography of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling claimed that Zhi, together with Zhang Pang, Li Chong, and others, had stirred up military sentiment—the account is given in the Biography of Yanling.

sentences.zh: 德宗怒，將誅贄等四人，會諫議大夫陽城等極言論奏，乃貶贄為忠州別駕。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong grew angry and was about to execute Zhi and the other four men; but Remonstrating Censor Yang Cheng and others remonstrated forcefully, and so Zhi was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong grew angry and was about to execute Zhi and the other three men, but Remonstrating Censor Yang Cheng and others remonstrated forcefully, and Zhi was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄初入翰林，特承德宗異顧，歌詩戲狎，朝夕陪遊。

translations.literal: When Zhi first entered the Hanlin Academy, he received Emperor Dezong's special and unusual favor—singing poems and playful intimacy, accompanying him morning and evening on his outings.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi first entered the Hanlin Academy, he received Emperor Dezong's special favor—singing poems in playful intimacy and accompanying him morning and evening on his outings.

sentences.zh: 及出居艱阻之中，雖有宰臣，而謀猷參決，多出於贄，故當時目為「內相」。

translations.literal: When they came to dwell in hardship and peril, though there were chief ministers, deliberation and decision mostly came from Zhi—hence people of the time called him the "Inner Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: When the court fell into hardship and peril, though chief ministers remained, deliberation and decision mostly came from Zhi—hence people of the time called him the "Inner Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 從幸山南，道途艱險，扈從不及，與帝相失，一夕不至，上喻軍士曰：「得贄者賞千金。」

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Shannan, the road was dangerous and perilous; the escort could not keep up, and he lost contact with the emperor—for one night he did not arrive, and the emperor told the soldiers: "Whoever finds Zhi will be rewarded with a thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the emperor to Shannan, the road was treacherous. The escort could not keep up, and he lost contact with the emperor. After one night without arrival, the emperor told the soldiers, "Whoever finds Zhi will be rewarded with a thousand gold.

sentences.zh: 翌日贄謁見，上喜形顏色，其寵待如此。

translations.literal: The next day Zhi came to audience; the emperor's delight showed on his face—such was the favor he received.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhi came to audience. The emperor's delight showed plainly on his face—such was the favor he received.

sentences.zh: 既與二吳不協，漸加浸潤，恩禮稍薄；

translations.literal: Once he fell out with the two Wus, slander gradually seeped in, and imperial favor and courtesy grew somewhat thin;
translations.idiomatic: Once he fell out with the two Wus, slander gradually seeped in, and imperial favor and courtesy grew somewhat thin.

sentences.zh: 及通玄敗，上知誣枉，遂復見用。

translations.literal: When Tong Xuan fell, the emperor knew he had been slandered and unjustly treated, and so Zhi was again employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Tongxuan fell, the emperor knew Zhi had been slandered and unjustly treated, and employed him again.

sentences.zh: 贄以受人主殊遇，不敢愛身，事有不可，極言無隱。

translations.literal: Zhi, having received the ruler's extraordinary favor, did not spare himself; when matters were wrong, he spoke out fully without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Having received the ruler's extraordinary favor, Zhi did not spare himself. When matters were wrong, he spoke out fully without concealment.

sentences.zh: 朋友規之，以為太峻，贄曰：「吾上不負天子，下不負吾所學，不恤其他。」

translations.literal: Friends admonished him, thinking him too harsh; Zhi said: "Above, I do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, I do not fail what I have learned—I care nothing for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Friends admonished him, thinking him too harsh. Zhi said, "Above, I do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, I do not fail what I have learned. I care nothing for the rest.

sentences.zh: 精於吏事，斟酌決斷，不失錙銖。

translations.literal: He was skilled in administrative affairs, weighing and deciding without missing so much as a mite.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in administrative affairs, weighing and deciding without missing so much as a mite.

sentences.zh: 嘗以「詞詔所出，中書舍人之職，軍興之際，促迫應務，權令學士代之；

translations.literal: He once argued that "edicts and decrees should issue from the Secretariat Drafters; in times of military emergency, pressed by urgent tasks, it was permitted to have academicians substitute;
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that "edicts and decrees belong to the Secretariat Drafters. In times of military emergency, pressed by urgent tasks, it was permitted to have Hanlin academicians substitute;

sentences.zh: 朝野乂寧，合歸職分，其命將相制詔，卻付中書行譴。」

translations.literal: When court and realm are at peace, they should return to their proper duties—the commands appointing generals and chancellors and the drafting of edicts should be turned back to the Secretariat for issuance.
translations.idiomatic: When court and realm are at peace, duties should return to their proper offices. Commands appointing generals and chancellors and the drafting of edicts should be turned back to the Secretariat for issuance.

sentences.zh: 又言「學士私臣，玄宗初令待詔，止於唱和文章而已」。

translations.literal: He also said, "Academicians are the ruler's private retainers. When Emperor Xuanzong first had them await edicts, it was only for composing matching verses and essays."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Academicians are the ruler's private retainers. When Emperor Xuanzong first had them await edicts, it was only for composing matching verses and essays."

sentences.zh: 物議是之。

translations.literal: Public opinion approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion approved this view.

sentences.zh: 德宗以贄指斥通微、通玄，故不可其奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, because Zhi's argument implicitly censured Tong Wei and Tong Xuan, did not approve his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, because Zhi's argument implicitly censured Wu Tongwei and Wu Tongxuan, did not approve his memorial.

sentences.zh: 贄在忠州十年，常閉關靜處，人不識其面，復避謗，不著書。

translations.literal: Zhi spent ten years in Zhongzhou, usually secluding himself in quiet retreat so that people did not know his face; he also avoided slander and wrote no books.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi spent ten years in Zhongzhou, usually secluding himself in quiet retreat so that people scarcely knew his face. He also avoided slander and wrote no books.

sentences.zh: 家居瘴鄉，人多癘疫，乃抄撮方書，為《陸氏集驗方》五十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: Living in a malarial region where many suffered pestilence, he copied and compiled medical prescription books, producing fifty scrolls of the Collected Verified Prescriptions of Master Lu, which circulated in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Living in a malarial region where many suffered pestilence, he copied and compiled medical prescription books into fifty scrolls of the Collected Verified Prescriptions of Master Lu, which circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 初，贄秉政，貶駕部員外郎李吉甫為明州長史，量移忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhi held power, he demoted Supervising Secretary of the Transport Office Li Jifu to Senior Administrator of Mingzhou, then transferred him to Prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhi held power, he had demoted Supervising Secretary of the Transport Office Li Jifu to Senior Administrator of Mingzhou, later transferring him to Prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄在忠州，與吉甫相遇，昆弟、門人鹹為贄憂，而吉甫忻然厚禮，都不銜前事，以宰相禮事之，猶恐其未信不安，日與贄相狎，若平生交契者。

translations.literal: When Zhi was in Zhongzhou and met Jifu, his brothers and disciples all worried for Zhi; but Jifu gladly treated him with great courtesy, harboring no resentment over past matters, serving him with the etiquette due a chief minister. Still fearing that Zhi might not believe him and feel uneasy, he daily kept close company with Zhi as if they had been intimate friends all their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi was in Zhongzhou and met Jifu, his brothers and disciples all worried for him. But Jifu gladly treated him with great courtesy, harboring no resentment over past matters and serving him with the etiquette due a chief minister. Still fearing that Zhi might not trust him and feel uneasy, he kept close company with Zhi daily, as if they had been intimate friends all their lives.

sentences.zh: 贄初猶慚懼，後乃深交。

translations.literal: At first Zhi was still ashamed and afraid; afterward they became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhi was still ashamed and afraid; afterward they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 時論以吉甫為長者。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion regarded Jifu as a man of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion regarded Jifu as a man of magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 後有薛延者，代吉甫為刺史，延朝辭日，德宗令宣旨慰安。

translations.literal: Later a man named Xue Yan replaced Jifu as prefect; on the day Yan took leave at court, Emperor Dezong ordered an edict of consolation and reassurance delivered.
translations.idiomatic: Later a man named Xue Yan replaced Jifu as prefect. On the day Yan took leave at court, Emperor Dezong ordered an edict of consolation and reassurance delivered to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 而韋臯累上表請以贄代己。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Wei Gao repeatedly submitted memorials asking that Zhi replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wei Gao repeatedly submitted memorials asking that Zhi replace him as his successor.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，與陽城、鄭余慶同詔征還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, an edict summoned him back together with Yang Cheng and Zheng Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, an edict summoned him back together with Yang Cheng and Zheng Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 詔未至而贄卒，時年五十二，贈兵部尚書，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Zhi died, aged fifty-two; he was posthumously granted Minister of War, with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, Zhi died at the age of fifty-two. He was posthumously granted Minister of War, with the posthumous title Xuan ("Declarer").

sentences.zh: 子簡禮，登進士第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: His son Jianli passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited to serve in commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianli passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited to serve in commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：近代論陸宣公，比漢之賈誼，而高邁之行，剛正之節，經國成務之要，激切仗義之心，初蒙天子重知，末塗淪躓，皆相類也。

translations.literal: The historian says: In recent times those who discuss Lu the Duke of Xuan compare him to Jia Yi of Han, and in lofty conduct, upright integrity, essentials of governing the state, and impassioned devotion to righteousness—first receiving the Son of Heaven's deep trust, then stumbling at the end—all are alike.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Recent commentators compare Lu the Duke of Xuan to Jia Yi of Han. In lofty conduct, upright integrity, mastery of statecraft, and impassioned devotion to righteousness—first receiving the emperor's deep trust, then stumbling at the end—the parallels are striking.

sentences.zh: 而誼止中大夫，贄及臺鉉，不為不遇矣。

translations.literal: Yet Yi reached only Grand Master of the Palace, while Zhi attained the chief ministry—not an instance of lack of recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jia Yi reached only Grand Master of the Palace, while Zhi attained the chief ministry—hardly a case of being unappreciated.

sentences.zh: 昔公孫鞅挾三策說秦王，淳于髡以隱語見齊君，從古以還，正言不易。

translations.literal: In old times Gongsun Yang brought three stratagems to persuade the King of Qin; Chunyu Kun used riddling speech to gain audience with the ruler of Qi—from antiquity onward, straight speech has never been easy.
translations.idiomatic: In old times Shang Yang brought three stratagems to persuade the King of Qin; Chunyu Kun used riddling speech to gain audience with the ruler of Qi. From antiquity onward, straight speech has never been easy.

sentences.zh: 昔周昭戒急論議，正為此也。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Zhao of Zhou warned against hasty disputation—precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Zhao of Zhou warned against hasty disputation—precisely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 贄居珥筆之列，調飪之地，欲以片心除眾弊，獨手遏群邪，君上不亮其誠，群小共攻其短，欲無放逐，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Zhi occupied the ranks of the brush-wearers and the place of seasoning words, wishing with a single heart to remove myriad abuses and with one hand to check the multitude of wicked—the ruler did not illuminate his sincerity, petty men together attacked his faults—to wish for no banishment, how could that be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi stood among the brush-wearers in the place where words are seasoned, wishing with a single heart to remove myriad abuses and with one hand to check the multitude of wicked. The ruler did not recognize his sincerity; petty men together attacked his faults. To expect no banishment—how could that be?

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱「其維哲人，告之話言」，又有「誨爾」、「聽我」之恨，此皆賢人君子，嘆言不見用也。

translations.literal: The Odes says, "How is he not a wise man! I tell him all my plans," and there is also the regret in "I instruct you" and "Listen to me"—all these are worthy gentlemen lamenting that their words were not employed.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "How is he not a wise man! I tell him all my plans," and also records the regret of "I instruct you" and "Listen to me"—all alike are worthy men lamenting that their counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 故堯咨禹拜，千載一時，攜手提耳，豈容易哉！

translations.literal: Therefore when Yao consulted and Yu bowed in acknowledgment, it was a moment of a thousand years; to take him by the hand and speak into his ear—how is that easy!
translations.idiomatic: When Yao consulted and Yu bowed in reply, it was a moment that comes once in a thousand years. To take a man by the hand and speak into his ear—is that easily achieved?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：良臣悟主，我有嘉猷。

translations.literal: Praise says: A good minister enlightens his lord; I have excellent plans.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: A worthy minister enlightens his sovereign; I have excellent counsel to offer.

sentences.zh: 多僻之君，為善不周。

translations.literal: A lord of many crooked ways does good without thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler prone to perversity does good without completing it.

sentences.zh: 忠言救失，啟沃曰讎。

translations.literal: Loyal words remedy faults; daily counsel meets with enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal words correct error, yet daily counsel is met with hostility.

sentences.zh: 勿貽天問，蒼昊悠悠。

translations.literal: Do not bring reproach from Heaven; the azure heavens are vast and far.
translations.idiomatic: Do not invite Heaven's rebuke; the azure sky stretches on without end.
